For a $k=5$ committee $n/k=2$ the $ {\rm EJR}$–requirement is

* $|S|\ge 2\ell\Rightarrow \exists i\in S\;|A_{i}\cap W|\ge \ell $

for $\ell =1,2,3,4$.  Up to $\ell =4$ every voter has
$|A_{i}|\ge 4$ and a voter can obtain $4$ approvals only with

* $8,9,10:\; \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$,
* $4,5:\; \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
* $6,7:\; \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$,
* $1:\;4$ members of $A_{1}$.

In particular with $|W\cap A_{1}|\le 2$ we have

* $|A_{1}\cap W|\le2$,
* $|A_{2}\cap W|\le2+{\bf 1}_{y_{2}\in W}\le3$,
* $|A_{8}\cap W|\le 2+{\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W}\le3$,
* $|A_{4}\cap W|\le3$,

so no voter can reach $4$ approvals.  Hence every $8$-set would
contain a voter with $<4$ approvals and $\ell =4$ would be violated.
Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge 3$ is necessary.

With $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ the only way to give a voter $4$ approvals in
every $8$-set is to make $8,9,10$ $4$-approved, i.e.

$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}\subseteq W$ .

Every $8$-set meets $\{8,9,10\}$, so
$|A_{8}\cap W|=4$ on every $8$–set and $\ell =4$ EJR is satisfied.
With the remaining place we must still give the $Y$–block
$\{4,5,6,7\}$ two representatives; this forces the fifth member to be
a $Y$–candidate, e.g. $y_{4}$.  Up to symmetry

$W_{0}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$

and any $EJR$ committee is of this form.  In particular

$|W\cap A_{1}|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3,$

and with $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ the $Y$–block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ can obtain at
most one representative, contradicting $\ell=2$ EJR.  Hence $3$ is the
only attainable value.

In the usual $1\!-\!4$ formulation of EJR this is
$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. the $E$ option.
The $3$ members are necessarily the three $x$’s, e.g. $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$,

customary $min\;3,\;max\;3$ statement.

With $n=10,\;k=5$ the EJR threshold is $2\ell$.  In particular
$\ell =4$ requires $8$ voters to contain a voter with $\ge4$ approvals and
$\ell =3$ requires $6$ voters to contain a voter with $\ge3$ approvals.

Put $c_{x}=|C\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{y_{1}}=|C\cap\{y_{1}\}|$,
$c_{z_{3}}=|C\cap\{z_{3}\}|$, $c_{y46}=|C\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$c_{z1},c_{z2}\in\{0,1\}$.
$I=|C\cap A_{1}|=c_{x}+c_{y_{1}}+c_{z_{3}}$ and
$|C|=c_{x}+c_{y46}+c_{z1}+c_{z2}+c_{y1}+c_{z3}+c_{y2}+c_{y3}=5$.

For the six voters $\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we need
$\max\{c_{x}+c_{y1}+c_{z3},c_{x}+c_{y2},c_{x}+c_{y3},c_{x}+c_{z1}\}\ge3$,
and for the 8-voter $\ell=4$ condition we need at least three voters with
$\ge4$ approvals.  The only way to obtain three distinct voters with
$\ge4$ approvals with five seats is

* $c_{x}=3$ and $c_{z1}=1$,

which gives $8,9,10$ the four approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}$ and
$|C\cap A_{1}|=3$.

The block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ needs a voter with $\ge2$ approvals, so the two
remaining seats after $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}$ must contain at least one
$y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$.  E.g. $C=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ is EJR:

etc., and every $6$-set and every $8$-set contains a voter with the
required number of approvals.

Hence $I=3$ is attainable.  $I\le2$ would give
$\max_{A}\le2$ and would make it impossible to have three distinct
voters with $\ge4$ approvals, contradicting the $\ell=4$ condition;
$I\ge4$ would leave $B=5-I\le1$ candidates outside $A_{1}$ and the four
voters $4,5,6,7$ could not obtain a $2$-approval voter.  Thus the EJR
feasible range is $I=3$.

So the minimum and the maximum number of voter-1-approved members are
both $3$.

The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all share x1,x2,x3.  With k=5 we have n/k=2 so |S|=6 forces ℓ=3 under EJR.  The only way to give one of those six voters 3 approvals without using three x’s is to use z1 for 8-10 or y2/y3 for 2/3, which still forces at least two of x1,x2,x3 to be in the committee. The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 are 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3}. Any EJR committee has to give a member of this group ≥3 approved seats. The only way to get three approvals for 2,3 or 8-10 without using three x’s is to use the private candidates y2/y3/z1 and that is not enough, so at least two of x1,x2,x3 have to be in the committee. One seat from that block is enough to keep the block represented together with the three x’s that satisfy the x-block, and the remaining three seats can be taken from A1. A. min 2, max 4

Reasoning

n =10, k=5 so a group of size ≥2ℓ needs ℓ representatives.

The 4 voters 4-7 all approve y4,y5,y6.  |S|=4 ≥2·2 so ℓ=2 applies.  Hence some voter in {4,5,6,7} must be approved in at least two places.  The cheapest way to do that is b≥1 y-candidates and, if b=1, also z1 for 4,5 or z2 for 6,7. In any EJR committee we therefore need at least one y-candidate from {y4,y5,y6} and in practice at least two y-candidates are forced once the other constraints are taken into account.

The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3. |S|=6 ≥2·3 so ℓ=3 applies.  Let a be the number of x1,x2,x3 in the committee and let c be 1 if z1 is in the committee.  Voter 8-10 are approved by a+c candidates and voter 1 is approved by a + {y1,z3}.  EJR for ℓ=3 is therefore satisfied as soon as a+c ≥3 or a+{y1,z3} ≥3.  The cheapest feasible satisfaction is a≥2 and c=0, i.e. at least two of x1,x2,x3 must be present and no committee can be EJR with a≤1.  Hence every EJR committee contains at least two x-candidates and voter 1, whose approval set contains the three x’s plus the private y1,z3, is therefore approved in at least those two x-candidates.  That gives the lower bound 2.

For the upper bound we can push the x-block to its maximum while still leaving room for the y-block required by voters 4-7.  The maximal x-content compatible with the y-requirement is a=3.  With a=3 we can still use one slot for the y-block and the remaining slot can be used for a private candidate of voter 1.  E.g. W={x1,x2,x3,y4,y1} is EJR: voters 4-7 are represented by y4 and, if needed, z1/z2, and voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 have voter 8-10 approved in three x-candidates.  Voter 1 is then approved in x1,x2,x3,y1, i.e. four of his five approved candidates.  Adding z3 instead of y1 would give five approvals for voter 1 but would leave the y-block with only one candidate and would break the ℓ=2 requirement for 4-7 once the private candidates are used up, so the attainable maximum under EJR is four approvals for voter 1, e.g. three x’s plus y1.  Hence the EJR range for voter 1 is min 2, max 4.

In either case at least two members of A1={x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} have to be present. The bound is tight e.g.

Wmax = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

The 6 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all have the common approval set {x1,x2,x3}. With n=10,k=5 we have n/k=2. 
|T|=6 ≥ 3·2 so the group is 3-cohesive. EJR therefore forces at least three of the common candidates into any EJR committee and the common set is exactly {x1,x2,x3}. Hence x1,x2,x3 are all three of them in every EJR committee.

The four voters 4,5,6,7 are 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6} and the 5-voter z1 coalition forces z1 to be present, so up to the usual proportionality the three x’s together with two y’s already exhaust the five seats. In the feasible EJR realisations the committee is therefore of the form {x1,x2,x3, y_a , y_b} with y_a,y_b∈{y4,y5,y6}.

Voter 1 approves {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3}. The y_a,y_b and any z1 that can be accommodated are never approved by voter 1, so the only approved members that can ever appear in an EJR committee are x1,x2,x3. Because the three x’s are forced, voter 1 gets exactly those three approved members in every EJR committee, i.e. 3 approved members in the minimum and in the maximum.

For a $k=5$ committee $n/k=2$ the $ {\rm EJR}$–requirement is

* $|S|\ge 2\ell\Rightarrow \exists i\in S\;|A_{i}\cap W|\ge \ell $

for $\ell =1,2,3,4$.  Up to $\ell =4$ every voter has
$|A_{i}|\ge 4$ and a voter can obtain $4$ approvals only with

* $8,9,10:\; \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$,
* $4,5:\; \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
* $6,7:\; \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$,
* $1:\;4$ members of $A_{1}$.

In particular with $|W\cap A_{1}|\le 2$ we have

* $|A_{1}\cap W|\le2$,
* $|A_{2}\cap W|\le2+{\bf 1}_{y_{2}\in W}\le3$,
* $|A_{8}\cap W|\le 2+{\bf 1}_{z_{1}\in W}\le3$,
* $|A_{4}\cap W|\le3$,

so no voter can reach $4$ approvals.  Hence every $8$-set would
contain a voter with $<4$ approvals and $\ell =4$ would be violated.
Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge 3$ is necessary.

With $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ the only way to give a voter $4$ approvals in
every $8$-set is to make $8,9,10$ $4$-approved, i.e.

$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}\subseteq W$ .

Every $8$-set meets $\{8,9,10\}$, so
$|A_{8}\cap W|=4$ on every $8$–set and $\ell =4$ EJR is satisfied.
With the remaining place we must still give the $Y$–block
$\{4,5,6,7\}$ two representatives; this forces the fifth member to be
a $Y$–candidate, e.g. $y_{4}$.  Up to symmetry

$W_{0}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$

and any $EJR$ committee is of this form.  In particular

$|W\cap A_{1}|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3,$

and with $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ the $Y$–block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ can obtain at
most one representative, contradicting $\ell=2$ EJR.  Hence $3$ is the
only attainable value.

In the usual $1\!-\!4$ formulation of EJR this is
$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. the $E$ option.
The $3$ members are necessarily the three $x$’s, e.g. $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$,
and $z_{1}$ is forced in every $EJR$ committee.  This is the
customary $min\;3,\;max\;3$ statement.

public_text.4:
E. min 3, max 3

With $n=10,\;k=5$ the EJR threshold is $2\ell$.  In particular
$\ell =4$ requires $8$ voters to contain a voter with $\ge4$ approvals and
$\ell =3$ requires $6$ voters to contain a voter with $\ge3$ approvals.

Put $c_{x}=|C\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c_{y_{1}}=|C\cap\{y_{1}\}|$,
$c_{z_{3}}=|C\cap\{z_{3}\}|$, $c_{y46}=|C\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$c_{z1},c_{z2}\in\{0,1\}$.
$I=|C\cap A_{1}|=c_{x}+c_{y_{1}}+c_{z_{3}}$ and
$|C|=c_{x}+c_{y46}+c_{z1}+c_{z2}+c_{y1}+c_{z3}+c_{y2}+c_{y3}=5$.

For the six voters $\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we need
$\max\{c_{x}+c_{y1}+c_{z3},c_{x}+c_{y2},c_{x}+c_{y3},c_{x}+c_{z1}\}\ge3$,
and for the 8-voter $\ell=4$ condition we need at least three voters with
$\ge4$ approvals.  The only way to obtain three distinct voters with
$\ge4$ approvals with five seats is

* $c_{x}=3$ and $c_{z1}=1$,

which gives $8,9,10$ the four approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}$ and
$|C\cap A_{1}|=3$.

The block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ needs a voter with $\ge2$ approvals, so the two
remaining seats after $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}$ must contain at least one
$y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}$.  E.g. $C=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1},y_{4}\}$ is EJR:
$1$ has $3$, $2,3$ have $3$, $8,9,10$ have $4$, $4,5$ have $z_{1},y_{4}$,
etc., and every $6$-set and every $8$-set contains a voter with the
required number of approvals.

Hence $I=3$ is attainable.  $I\le2$ would give
$\max_{A}\le2$ and would make it impossible to have three distinct
voters with $\ge4$ approvals, contradicting the $\ell=4$ condition;
$I\ge4$ would leave $B=5-I\le1$ candidates outside $A_{1}$ and the four
voters $4,5,6,7$ could not obtain a $2$-approval voter.  Thus the EJR
feasible range is $I=3$.

So the minimum and the maximum number of voter-1-approved members are
both $3$.

$n/k=2$ so $ |S|\ge2\ell$ . Hence

* $\ell=3$ on $S_X$ : $\max_{i\in S_X}|W\cap A_i|\ge3$
  with $|A_1\cap W|=a+b+c$, $|A_2\cap W|=a+f_2$, $|A_3\cap W|=a+f_3$, 
  $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+e_1$, $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, 
  $b=1_{y_1\in W}$, $c=1_{z_3\in W}$.

* $\ell=2$ on $S_Y$ : $\max_{i\in S_Y}|W\cap A_i|
  =y+\max(e_1,e_2)\ge2$ with $y=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, 
  $e_1=1_{z_1\in W}$, $e_2=1_{z_2\in W}$.

$|W|=5$, $t_1=|W\cap A_1|=a+b+c$, 
$a+b+c+f_2+f_3+y+e_1+e_2=5$.

The Y-condition forces at least two distinct members of 
$B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\subset A_1^{c}$ in $W$, so
$5-t_1\ge2$ and $t_1\le3$.

$a=0$ is impossible for the $\ell=3$ X-condition.
$a=1$ forces $b+c\ge2$, i.e. $t_1\ge3$, and with $b+c=2$ 
$f_2+f_3+y+e_1+e_2=2$ can be met e.g. $y=2$, giving $t_1=3$.

$a=2$ gives $t_1=2+b+c$ and $b+c+f_2+f_3+y+e_1+e_2=3$.
$b+c=0$ is feasible with $f_2=1$, $e_1=1$, $y=1$, e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$, $t_1=2$,
$|A_2\cap W|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=2$.

$b+c=1$ gives $t_1=3$ feasible e.g. $W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$.
$b+c=2$ would need $f_2+f_3+y+e_1+e_2=1$, which cannot satisfy 
$y+\max(e_1,e_2)\ge2$.

$a=3$ gives $b+c+f_2+f_3+y+e_1+e_2=2$. The Y-condition forces 
$y+\max(e_1,e_2)\ge2$, hence $b+c=0$ and $t_1=3$; e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$, $|A_1\cap W|=3$.

Hence $t_1\ge2$ and $t_1\le3$, with both extremes attainable under EJR.
Min $=2$, Max $=3$, i.e. option H. The claims of max $4$ or forced $t_1=3$
rest on an incorrect Y-requirement or on a non-existent $\ell=4$ cohesive
group.

1.text:
The only groups that can be binding for $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  It is $3$-cohesive and for $\ell =3$ EJR needs
$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\ge3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  It is $2$-cohesive and EJR needs
$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|A_{i}\cap W|\ge2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{1}=[z_{1}\in W]$, $z_{2}=[z_{2}\in W]$.
For voter 1
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b$, $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$.

$|W\cap A_{4}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=p+z_{2}$ so the $2$-cohesive
$S_{Y}$ requires
\[
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2,
\tag{Y}
\]
i.e. at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
Hence with $|W|=5$
\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b\le 5-|W\cap B|\le3 .
\tag{1}
\]

For $S_{X}$ 
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+[y_{2}\in W]$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+[y_{3}\in W]$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1}$ and $|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b$.  EJR for $\ell=3$ is
\[
a+\max\{b,[y_{2}\in W],[y_{3}\in W],z_{1}\}\ge3 .
\tag{X}
\]

$a=0$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$; $a=1$ gives (X) only
with $b=2$, i.e. $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$.  Hence $a+b\ge2$ in every EJR
committee and $a+b=1$ is impossible.  With $a=2,\;b=0$ we can satisfy
(X) with $[y_{2}\in W]=1$ or $z_{1}=1$ and (Y) with $p=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W_{\min}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$
are $3$- and $2$-represented.

The upper bound (1) is attainable.  With $a=3,\;b=0$ we can take
$p=2$, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|A_{2}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$, so EJR holds and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is maximal.  $a+b=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$,
contradicting (Y), and $a+b=5$ is impossible.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ approved seats and
can meet him in at most $3$ approved seats, and both extremes are
realised.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. option H.

11.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ the EJR threshold is $|S|\ge 2\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $\ell =3$ is active.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
  $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
  $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.
  Hence $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ and in particular $a\ge2$ unless
  $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  So $ |W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and
  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ is impossible.  With $a=2$ the $\ell=3$ witness can be
  obtained with a private candidate,
  e.g. $y_{2}$ for voter 2.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $\ell =2$ is active.  Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
  $c={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.  Then
  $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+b$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+c$ and
  $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=p+\max(b,c)\ge2$.
  $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
  $YZ=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, so the two approvals required for
  $S_{Y}$ must be taken from $YZ$.  Hence
  $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

  $$|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3 .$$

The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, 
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.  So $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

The bound $2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

hence $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=0,1$ would give $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$, so
the $\ell=3$ requirement for $S_{X}$ fails.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,$$

i.e. voter 1 can be met in $2$ approved seats at a minimum and in $3$
approved seats at a maximum.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.  In
particular a committee with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},
y_{1},y_{4}\}$, gives $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$ and violates the
$2$-cohesive $Y$-block.

6.text:
For $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ an $\ell$–cohesive set is $|S|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR is

$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell$.

The only non–trivial common intersections are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\},\;|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $|S_{X}|\ge 2\cdot 3$ so $\ell_{X}=3$ is active.  Put
  $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
  $e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,
  $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$.

  \[
  |W\cap A_{1}|=a+u,\qquad
  |W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2},\qquad
  |W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3},\qquad
  |W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1},
  \]
  and EJR for $S_{X}$ is
  $a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3$.  \tag{1}

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\},\;|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $|S_{Y}|\ge 2\cdot2$ so $\ell_{Y}=2$ is active.  Put
  $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
  $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$ and

  $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$. \tag{2}

$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$, so (2) forces at
least two seats of $W$ to lie outside $A_{1}$.  With $|W|=5$,

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u\le 5-2 =3,
\]

and the bound is attainable.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$–represented by $2,8,\dots$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$–represented
by $4,5$. Hence $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=0,1$ is impossible from (1): $a=0$ gives
$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$; $a=1$ forces $u=2$ for (1) and
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  The smallest feasible is $a=2,u=0$.
With $a=2$ we can satisfy (1) with $e_{2}=1$ or $z_{1}=1$ and (2) with
$p\ge2$ or $p=1,z_{1}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are EJR–satisfied.  Hence
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and $1$ is unattainable.

The $\ell=4$ argument invoked for the $\min= \max =3$ claim is
spurious: there is no $S$ with $|S|\ge 8$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge4$,
so $\ell=4$ EJR imposes no restriction.  The committees
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ etc. used for a claimed $\max 4$
give $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$, violating (2) for $S_{Y}$.

Hence under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both attainable.  This is
option H, min 2 max 3.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: min 2 max 3, i.e. option H.

Put $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  An $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ and EJR requires
$\exists i\in S:|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

*$X$-block.* $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_X|=6$,
$\bigcap_{S_X}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
Let $t=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $p=[y_1\in W]+[z_3\in W]$,
$e=[y_2\in W]\vee[y_3\in W]$, $z_1=[z_1\in W]$.
Then 
$|W\cap A_1|=t+p$, $|W\cap A_2|=t+[y_2]$, $|W\cap A_8|=t+z_1$, etc., 
and EJR for $\ell=3$ is
$t+\max\{p,e,z_1\}\ge3$.                                           (1)

*$Y$-block.* $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_Y|=4$,
$\bigcap_{S_Y}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.
Let $y=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $z_1,z_2\in\{0,1\}$.
$|W\cap A_4|=y+z_1$, $|W\cap A_6|=y+z_2$ and EJR for $\ell=2$ is
$y+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$.                                           (2)
$A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$, so (2) forces
$|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ with $YZ=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$.

Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_1|=t+p\le5-2=3$

and (1) is satisfiable.  The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_1|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_2|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_4|=2$, so $S_X$ is $3$-represented and $S_Y$ is $2$-represented.

$t+p=4$ is impossible.  $t+p=4$ needs $t=3,p=1$ or $t=2,p=2$, whence
$q+y+r=1$ with $q=[y_2]+[y_3]$, $r=z_1+z_2$, $y$ as above.  Then
$y+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  So $\max|W\cap A_1|=3$.

For the minimum $t+p\ge2$.  $t+p=0,1$ makes (1) impossible:
$t=0$ gives $\max_i|W\cap A_i|\le2$, $t=1$ needs $p=2$ to reach $3$,
i.e. $t+p\ge3$.  $t+p=2$ is attainable with $t=2,p=0$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_2|=t+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_4|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.  Likewise
$\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ gives $|W\cap A_1|=2$ and
$|W\cap A_8|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=3$.

Hence under the usual approval EJR 
$2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$,
the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both attainable.  This is the
range quoted as option H.  Committees claimed to give voter 1 four
approvals, e.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$, violate (2) because
$y+\max\{z_1,z_2\}=1<2$ and the $Y$-block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ is not
$2$-represented.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The only binding cohesive groups are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $|S_{X}|\ge 2\ell$ gives $\ell=3$, i.e. 
  $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$.
  With $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, 
  $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
  $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, 
  $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $|S_{Y}|\ge2\ell$ gives $\ell=2$, i.e. 
  $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$.
  With $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $c={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$,
  $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+b$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+c$.
  Hence $p+\max\{b,c\}\ge2$.

$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$, so the two
candidates needed for $S_{Y}$ lie outside $A_{1}$.  Consequently
$|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ with $YZ=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$|W|=5$ gives

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap YZ|\le3$.

The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ are EJR-satisfied.
$t=4$ would need $|W\cap YZ|\le1$ and would make
$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le1$, impossible. Hence
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

For the lower bound write $t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.
$t=0,1$ gives $a\le1$ and $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$, violating
the $\ell=3$ requirement for $S_{X}$.  $t=2$ is feasible, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are EJR-satisfied.  Hence $t\ge2$ and $t=2$ is
attainable.

Thus an EJR 5-committee can meet voter 1 in 2 approved seats and can meet
him in at most 3 approved seats,

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3,$

i.e. option H, min 2 max 3.

10.text:
The only $\ell$-cohesive groups which can be binding are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$n/k=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$ ,     $\ell =3$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, 
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and

$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 2$ ,     $\ell =2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}
+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $t_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$,
$y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{1},z_{2}\in\{0,1\}$.
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$.

For $S_{Y}$

$|A_{4}\cap W|=y+z_{1}$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=y+z_{2}$,
hence $y+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$, so at least two seats of $W$
lie outside $A_{1}$.  With $|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t_{1}\le 5-2=3$,

and $t_{1}=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

Hence $\max t_{1}=3$.

For $S_{X}$

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|A_{3}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1}$.

$a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le 2$, $a=1$ forces
$u=2$ to reach $3$, i.e. $t_{1}\ge3$.  The smallest feasible
is $a=2,u=0$.  With $a=2$ we can have $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|=3$
by using a private candidate $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}$ and we can still
satisfy $S_{Y}$ with two $Y$ seats, e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

$t_{1}=1$ would need $a\le1$ and then $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$,
so $t_{1}=1,0$ are impossible.  Thus $t_{1}\ge2$.

Consequently an EJR $5$–committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ approved
seats and in at most $3$ approved seats, and both bounds are attained.

Min $=2$, Max $=3$, i.e. option H.

16.text:
The two relevant $\ell$-cohesive groups are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6=3n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
   =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Hence for $\ell =3$
  \[
  \max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3 .
  \tag{1}
  \]
  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
  $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=
  a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, etc.  In particular (1) is impossible with $a=0$
  and it is impossible with $a=1$, $u\le 1$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4=2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
  =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
  $b_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $b_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
  \[
  \max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=p+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\ge 2 .
  \tag{2}
  \]
  Hence at least two members of

$\ell =2$ is active.  Put $h=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$g={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$|A_{4}\cap W|=h+f$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=h+g$ and

$h+\max\{f,g\}\ge2,\qquad h+f\ge1,\qquad h+g\ge1\tag{2}$

together with $a+f\ge1$ from $\{8,9,10\}$.

Put $t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b+c$.  Then

$|W|=a+b+c+d+e+f+g+h=5$, i.e. $t+d+e+f+g+h=5$ .

From (2) $h\ge1$ and $h+\max\{f,g\}\ge2$, hence $f+g+h\ge2$.
Hence

$t=5-(d+e+f+g+h)\le5-2=3$,

and $t=3$ is attainable e.g. with $a=3,\;b=c=d=e=0,\;h=2$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|A_{1}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$, so (1)–(2)
hold.

For the lower bound $t=1$ gives $a\le1$ and $\max\{a+d,a+e,a+f\}\le2$,
contradicting (1); $t=0$ is impossible for the same reason.
$t=2$ is feasible.  E.g. $a=2,b=c=0$, $d=1,f=1,h=1$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},z_{1},y_{4}\}$,

$|A_{1}\cap W|=2$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=a+d=3$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+f=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W|=h+f=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is
$2$-represented.  Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable,
and $1,0$ are impossible.

Thus under EJR

$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

the $2$ being attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and the
$3$ by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.  This is option H,
min 2 max 3.

4.text:
The $n/k=2$ threshold is $|S|\ge 2\ell $.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $\ell =3$ is active.  Put
  $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=|W\cap\{y_{1},z_{3}\}|$,
  $e_{2}= {\bf1}_{y_{2}},e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$.
  Then
  $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3}$,
  $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1}$ and
  $a+\max\{b,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3$ is EJR for $S_{X}$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  Put $y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  EJR for $\ell =2$ is
  $\max\{y+z_{1},y+z_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $y\ge1$ and $y+{\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}}\ge2$.
  In particular $W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}\ne\varnothing$ and
  $W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}\ne\varnothing$, so at least two
  places of $W$ lie outside $A_{1}$.

Write $r=y+z_{1}+z_{2}\ge2$ and $s=e_{2}+e_{3}$.
$|W|=a+b+s+y+z_{1}+z_{2}=5$, hence
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b=5-r-s$.

$r_{\min}=2$ is obtained for $y=1,\;z_{1}+z_{2}=1$ and $s_{\min}=0$, so

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3$,

and $3$ is attained, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.

$a+\max\{b,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$ gives $a+b\ge2$.  With $a=2,b=0$
the condition is $ \max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$, which is compatible
with $y\ge1$, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ are both EJR.
$a+b=1$ would give $a+\max\{b,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\le2$, contradicting
the $\ell=3$ requirement for $S_{X}$; $a+b=0$ is impossible.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter 1 in $2$ approved seats and
can meet him in at most $3$ approved seats, and both bounds are tight.

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2,\;\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$ i.e. option H.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with the group on the lower bound.  $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ so some $i\in S_{X}$ has to meet $W$ in $\ge3$ places.  Voters $2,3,8,9,10$ can only get a third approval from $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ on top of the $x$’s, so an EJR committee has to contain at least two $x$’s and the two $x$’s are already approved by voter 1.  The committee

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{2}|=3$ and $|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $2$ is attainable and $1$ is impossible.  Min=2 is solid.

On the upper side the usual $ |W\cap YZ|\ge2$ counting is too pessimistic because the same candidate can do work for both the $X$–block and the $Y$–block.  $z_{1}$ is approved by $4,5$ and it is the cheapest way to give $8,9,10$ their third approval together with two $x$’s.  Hence the seat $z_{1}$ can be counted once for the $X$ requirement and once for the $Y$ requirement.

With that double use we can keep the three $x$’s that $S_{X}$ wants and still leave room for a private $A_{1}$ candidate.  E.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$

gives
* $|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$,
* $v_{2}$ has $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}=3$, so the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is satisfied,
* $v_{4}$ has $y_{4}$ and the $Y$–block $\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and the $z_{1}$–overlap with $8,9,10$ is the usual way the $X$–block and the $Y$–block are simultaneously covered, so the $\ell=2$ requirement for $\{4,5,6,7\}$ is met.

In practice the cheapest way to meet the $Y$–block is $y_{4}+z_{1}$ for voters $4,5$ and $y_{4}$ together with the $x$’s for the $X$–block, so one $Y$ seat plus the shared $z_{1}$ seat is enough to free the remaining three seats for $A_{1}$.  That is why the bound $|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ obtained by subtracting two completely disjoint outside seats from $5$ is not tight.  With the shared use of $z_{1}$ we can realise four $A_{1}$ approvals for voter 1 and we cannot realise five because the $Y$–block would then be empty.

Hence an EJR $5$–committee can give voter 1 $2$ approved members and can give him $4$ approved members.  That is min $2$, max $4$, i.e. option A.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the min 2 side and I think the lower bound is solid.

$n/k=2$. $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$–cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
For $i\in S_{X}$
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$ with $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
Hence $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ forces $a\ge2$ unless
${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=1$.  With $a=2$ and $y_{2}\in W$ we get the
usual witness

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so the $3$–cohesive $S_{X}$ and the $2$–cohesive $Y$–block are both
satisfied.  $a=0,1$ is impossible for the $3$–cohesive requirement, so
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable.  That part is settled.

The max argument of the $H$ bloc double counts the $z$ candidates.
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}=\varnothing$, so the only candidates that
can represent the $Y$ side are $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
The $4$–voter set $\{4,5,6,7\}$ does not have a common $2$–set which is
disjoint from the $X$–witness.  The maximal $2$–cohesive subsets are
$\{4,5\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and
$\{6,7\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$; each of them
is $1$–cohesive.  In practice the $2$–cohesive requirement for the
$Y$ side can be met by one $y$ candidate together with the $z$
candidate that is already needed for the $X$–witness $8,9,10$.

Indeed $z_{1}$ is outside $A_{1}$ but it is approved by $8,9,10$ and by
$4,5$.  With $a=3$ we can therefore use $z_{1}$ to give the
$X$–block its third approval and at the same time give the $\{4,5\}$
pair its required approval.  The remaining $Y$ need for $\{6,7\}$ is
then covered by the single $y$ that is present to keep the committee
size $5$.

Hence one seat outside $A_{1}$ is sufficient to keep both
cohesive families happy and the $X$–block can be taken with three
$x$’s.  E.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$.

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}=3+1=4$.  Voter $1$ is approved in
$x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$.  $8,9,10$ are approved in
$x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}$, i.e. $4\ge3$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$–represented.
$4,5$ are approved in $z_{1}$ and the $y$–block is represented through
the $y$–candidate that the $2$–cohesive condition for $\{4,5,6,7\}$
allows to be identified with the same $z_{1}$ witness used for the
$X$–block.  Up to the usual $y_{4}/y_{5}$ symmetry this is the
conventional extremal committee
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, which gives voter $1$ the four
approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ and still leaves a $y$ representative
for the $Y$ side while the $X$–block is witnessed by $1,2,3$ or
$8,9,10$.

Thus two approvals for voter $1$ cannot be avoided and four approvals
can be attained.  The attainable range under EJR is therefore
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, i.e. the $A$ option.
The claimed upper bound $3$ comes from counting the $z$ seat twice,
once for the $X$ witness and once for the $Y$ witness, whereas the
$z$ seat can be shared.  That sharing is what allows the three $x$’s
plus $y_{1}$ to sit together with a single outside candidate and still
be EJR.

public_text.1:
The only groups that can be binding for $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  It is $3$-cohesive and for $\ell =3$ EJR needs
$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\ge3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  It is $2$-cohesive and EJR needs
$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|A_{i}\cap W|\ge2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b=[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{1}=[z_{1}\in W]$, $z_{2}=[z_{2}\in W]$.
For voter 1
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b$, $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$.

$|W\cap A_{4}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=p+z_{2}$ so the $2$-cohesive
$S_{Y}$ requires
\[
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2,
\tag{Y}
\]
i.e. at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
Hence with $|W|=5$
\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b\le 5-|W\cap B|\le3 .
\tag{1}
\]

For $S_{X}$ 
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+[y_{2}\in W]$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+[y_{3}\in W]$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1}$ and $|A_{1}\cap W|=a+b$.  EJR for $\ell=3$ is
\[
a+\max\{b,[y_{2}\in W],[y_{3}\in W],z_{1}\}\ge3 .
\tag{X}
\]

$a=0$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$; $a=1$ gives (X) only
with $b=2$, i.e. $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$.  Hence $a+b\ge2$ in every EJR
committee and $a+b=1$ is impossible.  With $a=2,\;b=0$ we can satisfy
(X) with $[y_{2}\in W]=1$ or $z_{1}=1$ and (Y) with $p=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W_{\min}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$
are $3$- and $2$-represented.

The upper bound (1) is attainable.  With $a=3,\;b=0$ we can take
$p=2$, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|A_{2}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$, so EJR holds and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is maximal.  $a+b=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$,
contradicting (Y), and $a+b=5$ is impossible.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter $1$ in $2$ approved seats and
can meet him in at most $3$ approved seats, and both extremes are
realised.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. option H.
public_text.11:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ the EJR threshold is $|S|\ge 2\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $\ell =3$ is active.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
  $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
  $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.
  Hence $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$ and in particular $a\ge2$ unless
  $y_{1},z_{3}\in W$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  So $ |W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and
  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ is impossible.  With $a=2$ the $\ell=3$ witness can be
  obtained with a private candidate,
  e.g. $y_{2}$ for voter 2.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $\ell =2$ is active.  Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
  $c={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.  Then
  $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+b$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+c$ and
  $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=p+\max(b,c)\ge2$.
  $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
  $YZ=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, so the two approvals required for
  $S_{Y}$ must be taken from $YZ$.  Hence
  $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

  $$|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3 .$$

The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, 
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.  So $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

The bound $2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

hence $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=0,1$ would give $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$, so
the $\ell=3$ requirement for $S_{X}$ fails.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,$$

i.e. voter 1 can be met in $2$ approved seats at a minimum and in $3$
approved seats at a maximum.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.  In
particular a committee with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},
y_{1},y_{4}\}$, gives $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$ and violates the
$2$-cohesive $Y$-block.
public_text.6:
For $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ an $\ell$–cohesive set is $|S|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR is

$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge \ell$.

The only non–trivial common intersections are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\},\;|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
  $|S_{X}|\ge 2\cdot 3$ so $\ell_{X}=3$ is active.  Put
  $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
  $e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,
  $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$.

  \[
  |W\cap A_{1}|=a+u,\qquad
  |W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2},\qquad
  |W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3},\qquad
  |W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1},
  \]
  and EJR for $S_{X}$ is
  $a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3$.  \tag{1}

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\},\;|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
  $|S_{Y}|\ge 2\cdot2$ so $\ell_{Y}=2$ is active.  Put
  $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
  $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$ and

  $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$. \tag{2}

$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$, so (2) forces at
least two seats of $W$ to lie outside $A_{1}$.  With $|W|=5$,

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u\le 5-2 =3,
\]

and the bound is attainable.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$–represented by $2,8,\dots$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$–represented
by $4,5$. Hence $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=0,1$ is impossible from (1): $a=0$ gives
$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$; $a=1$ forces $u=2$ for (1) and
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  The smallest feasible is $a=2,u=0$.
With $a=2$ we can satisfy (1) with $e_{2}=1$ or $z_{1}=1$ and (2) with
$p\ge2$ or $p=1,z_{1}=1$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are EJR–satisfied.  Hence
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and $1$ is unattainable.

The $\ell=4$ argument invoked for the $\min= \max =3$ claim is
spurious: there is no $S$ with $|S|\ge 8$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge4$,
so $\ell=4$ EJR imposes no restriction.  The committees
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ etc. used for a claimed $\max 4$
give $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$, violating (2) for $S_{Y}$.

Hence under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both attainable.  This is
option H, min 2 max 3.
public_text.3:
min 2 max 3, i.e. option H.

Put $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  An $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell$ and EJR requires
$\exists i\in S:|W\cap A_i|\ge\ell$.

*$X$-block.* $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_X|=6$,
$\bigcap_{S_X}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
Let $t=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $p=[y_1\in W]+[z_3\in W]$,
$e=[y_2\in W]\vee[y_3\in W]$, $z_1=[z_1\in W]$.
Then 
$|W\cap A_1|=t+p$, $|W\cap A_2|=t+[y_2]$, $|W\cap A_8|=t+z_1$, etc., 
and EJR for $\ell=3$ is
$t+\max\{p,e,z_1\}\ge3$.                                           (1)

*$Y$-block.* $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_Y|=4$,
$\bigcap_{S_Y}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.
Let $y=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $z_1,z_2\in\{0,1\}$.
$|W\cap A_4|=y+z_1$, $|W\cap A_6|=y+z_2$ and EJR for $\ell=2$ is
$y+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$.                                           (2)
$A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$, so (2) forces
$|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ with $YZ=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$.

Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_1|=t+p\le5-2=3$

and (1) is satisfiable.  The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_1|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_2|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_4|=2$, so $S_X$ is $3$-represented and $S_Y$ is $2$-represented.

$t+p=4$ is impossible.  $t+p=4$ needs $t=3,p=1$ or $t=2,p=2$, whence
$q+y+r=1$ with $q=[y_2]+[y_3]$, $r=z_1+z_2$, $y$ as above.  Then
$y+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  So $\max|W\cap A_1|=3$.

For the minimum $t+p\ge2$.  $t+p=0,1$ makes (1) impossible:
$t=0$ gives $\max_i|W\cap A_i|\le2$, $t=1$ needs $p=2$ to reach $3$,
i.e. $t+p\ge3$.  $t+p=2$ is attainable with $t=2,p=0$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_2|=t+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_4|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.  Likewise
$\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ gives $|W\cap A_1|=2$ and
$|W\cap A_8|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=3$.

Hence under the usual approval EJR 
$2\le|W\cap A_1|\le3$,
the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both attainable.  This is the
range quoted as option H.  Committees claimed to give voter 1 four
approvals, e.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$, violate (2) because

The only $\ell$-cohesive groups which can be binding are

$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$n/k=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and

The two relevant $\ell$-cohesive groups are

  \[
  \max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3 .
  \tag{1}
  \]

  $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=
  a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, etc.  In particular (1) is impossible with $a=0$
  and it is impossible with $a=1$, $u\le 1$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4=2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
  =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
  $b_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $b_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
  \[
  \max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=p+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\ge 2 .
  \tag{2}
  \]
  Hence at least two members of
  $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ are required in $W$ and
  $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ with $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.
  Consequently
  \[
  |W\cap B|\ge 2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
  |W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3 .
  \]

The bound is attainable, e.g.
\[
W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$ and
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.  Hence $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$;

For the lower bound $a+u=|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.  $a+u=0,1$ makes (1)

\]
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$ and
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and

Hence under EJR
\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]
i.e. the smallest possible number of voter-1 approved seats is $2$ and
the largest possible number is $3$.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.

The only $\ell$–cohesive groups which matter are

I think the min is indeed 2 and the max is 4, i.e. option A.

The six voter X-block $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and the four voter Y-block $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  $n/k=2$.

For the lower bound $w_{X}=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.  The cheapest way to give a member of $S_{X}$ three approvals without using $y_{1},z_{3}$ of voter 1 is to give 8,9,10 two $x$’s together with $z_{1}$, or to give 2,3 two $x$’s together with $y_{2},y_{3}$.  Hence any EJR committee needs $w_{X}\ge 2$.  Those two $x$’s are in $A_{1}$ and the $S_{Y}$ requirement can be met with the two $y$’s.

E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{8}|=x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}=3$ so $S_{X}$ is 3-represented,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}=3$ so $S_{Y}$ is 2-represented.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ is impossible because then $w_{X}\le1$ and no member of $S_{X}$ can reach three approvals.  So $\min =2$.

The $YZ$ bound used for the max is too strong.  $S_{Y}$ can be represented with a candidate that also helps $S_{X}$.  In particular $z_{1}\in A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is common to the two blocks, so a seat spent on $z_{1}$ counts for both constraints.  Hence the two seats needed for $S_{Y}$ are not disjoint from the seats needed for $S_{X}$.

With $w_{X}=3$ we can let voter 1 be the $S_{X}$ witness.  Put $y_{1}\in W$ to use the private part of $A_{1}$ and keep one $y$ seat for $S_{Y}$.  Then

$W_{\max}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$

gives

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}=3$ so $S_{X}$ is 3-represented,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=y_{4}$ and the $y$–block is represented in the usual EJR sense by the common $y$’s; with the $z_{1}$ overlap available in the $S_{X}$ witness the $S_{Y}$ 2-requirement is met.

Up to symmetry the three $x$’s can be kept and one private $A_{1}$ candidate can be added, leaving a single $y$ seat for $S_{Y}$.  That is the extremal $A_{1}$ content.  Five approvals for voter 1 would leave no room for $S_{Y}$ at all, so max $<5$.

Hence under EJR we can realise $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and we can realise $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, with 2 the smallest attainable and 4 the largest attainable.  That is min 2, max 4.

I agree with the consensus that the lower bound is 2 and I think the upper bound is 4, i.e. option A.

Put $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and let $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $6$ voters, $\bigcap S_{X}=X$.  With $n/k=2$
$S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive so some $i\in S_{X}$ must have $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$.
For $i=2,3,8,9,10$ we have $|W\cap A_{i}|=|W\cap X|$ up to the private
$y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}$.  Hence $|W\cap X|\ge 2$ in every EJR committee and
the two $x$’s are already approved by voter 1.  With $|W\cap X|=2$ we can
give the $3$-requirement to $2$ by $y_{2}$, to $8$ by $z_{1}$, etc.  The
cheapest realisation is e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ are EJR satisfied.  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$
would give $|W\cap X|\le 1$ and $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$,
hence $ |W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable.

For the upper side let $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $S_{Y}$ is
$4$ voters with $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and is $2$-cohesive.
A $2$-approval for a $Y$ voter can be obtained either by two $y$’s or by
one $y$ together with the private $z$ of the same pair $\{4,5\}$ or
$\{6,7\}$.  In particular one $y$ candidate is enough to start the
representation of $S_{Y}$ and the second approval can be supplied by the
$z$ candidate that is already useful for the $X$-block, e.g. $z_{1}$ for
$8,9,10$.

Hence the $S_{Y}$ requirement can be met with essentially one net seat
taken from $A_{1}^{c}$.  With $|W|=5$ that leaves four seats that can be
taken from $A_{1}$.  The three $x$’s are forced by $S_{X}$ and the fourth
seat can be taken from the private part $\{y_{1},z_{3}\}$ of voter 1.
For instance

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$

is EJR: $v_{2}$ has $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$, $v_{8}$ has $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented, and $v_{4},v_{5}$ have the $y$ seat
$y_{4}$ together with the $z$ seat that is available for the $X$-block,
giving the required $2$-representation for $S_{Y}$.  In $W_{max}$

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=|\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}\}|=4$,

and the $X$-block is satisfied by the three $x$’s.  Up to symmetry the
same is obtained with $z_{3}$ in place of $y_{1}$.  Five $A_{1}$ seats are
impossible because $S_{Y}$ would then be empty.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can meet voter 1 in $2$ approved members and
can meet him in $4$ approved members, with $2$ as the least attainable
and $4$ as the greatest attainable number.  That is min $2$, max $4$.

The $n/k=2$ and $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$YZ=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $t_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}
+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$ and $b=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+t_{1}$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  $S_{X}$ is $3$–cohesive, so
\[
\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3,
\tag{1}
\]
i.e. $a+\max \{t_{1},{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$.
In particular $a\ge2$ unless $t_{1}=2$, and $a+b\ge2$ is necessary for
(1).

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  $S_{Y}$ is $2$–cohesive, so with
$y=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$
\[
\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=y+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2 .
\tag{2}
\]
Hence $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ and $A_{1}\cap YZ=\varnothing$ gives
$|W\cap A_{1}|=b\le5-2=3$.

$b=3$ is attainable, e.g.
$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W_{max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.  $b=4$
would need $\ge3$ members of $A_{1}$ and at most one member of $YZ$,
contradicting (2).  Hence $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$b=1$ is impossible for (1): with $a+t_{1}=1$ we have $a\le1$ and

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{2}|=x_{1},x_{2},y_{2}=3$,

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can give voter $1$ $2$ approved seats and can
give him at most $3$ approved seats, and $0,1,4$ are impossible. 
$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. option H.

Once $z_{1}$ is present for the $X$-block it already supplies the second approval for $4,5$. Hence the effective cost of the $Y_{4}$ requirement is one $y$ seat that is essentially disjoint from $A_{1}$; $z_{1}$ is shared with the $X$-block.

With that sharing we can keep three $x$’s in $W$ and still meet $Y_{4}$ with a single $y$. For example
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$, 
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ from the three $x$’s, and $4,5$ are represented by $y_{4}$ together with the $z$ that is normally used for the $X$-block. gives $|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{2}|=3$ and $|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $2$ is attainable and $1$ is impossible.  Min=2 is solid.

Hence the seat $z_{1}$ can be counted once for the $X$ requirement and once for the $Y$ requirement.

With the shared use of $z_{1}$ we can realise four $A_{1}$ approvals for voter 1 and we cannot realise five because the $Y$–block would then be empty.

disjoint from the $X$–witness.  The maximal $2$–cohesive subsets are
$\{4,5\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and
$\{6,7\}$ with $\bigcap A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$; each of them

$Y$ side can be met by one $y$ candidate together with the $z$
candidate that is already needed for the $X$–witness $8,9,10$.

Indeed $z_{1}$ is outside $A_{1}$ but it is approved by $8,9,10$ and by
$4,5$.  With $a=3$ we can therefore use $z_{1}$ to give the
$X$–block its third approval and at the same time give the $\{4,5\}$
pair its required approval.  The remaining $Y$ need for $\{6,7\}$ is

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}=3+1=4$.  Voter $1$ is approved in

allows to be identified with the same $z_{1}$ witness used for the

conventional extremal committee
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, which gives voter $1$ the four
approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ and still leaves a $y$ representative

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$\ell_{Y}=2$ is active.  With $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.  The same is obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$,
$W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with both extremes realisable.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.

The $\ell=4$ $8$-voter condition and the claimed $z_{1}$ sharing that
would give $\max 4$ do not give an EJR committee: the $Y$-block would
still have $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$.

16.text:
For $n=10,k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.
The only $\ell$–cohesive sets with a non–empty common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$ and EJR requires  

  $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$,

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$ and EJR requires  

  $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u=:t$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and

$|W\cap A_{4}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6}|=p+z_{2}$,

so $S_{Y}$ is EJR iff

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$,
\tag{Y}

and therefore $|W\cap B|\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-|W\cap B|\le 3$,

and $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ is exact, so the two seats needed for $S_{Y}$
are completely outside $A_{1}$.

For $S_{X}$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1}$,

hence

$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge3$.          \tag{X}

$a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$; $a=1$ forces $u=2$ and
$t\ge3$.  The smallest feasible $S_{X}$ requirement is $a=2,u=0$.
With $a=2$ we can obtain the $3$-witness by a private candidate
$y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$.

Hence $t\ge2$ and $t=1,0$ are impossible for (X).

The two bounds are tight.

*Upper.*  $a=3,u=0,p=2$ gives

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.
$t=4$ would need $|W\cap B|=1$, whence $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$ and
(Y) is violated; e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$.  The same holds for the $z_{1}$-sharing
examples $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$.  Hence $\max t=3$.

*Lower.*  $a=2,u=0$ with $e_{2}=1$, $p=2$ gives

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ are EJR satisfied.  The same is obtained with
$z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$.

Thus every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

and both extremes are attainable.  In particular
$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. option H.
The claimed $t=4$ committees fail (Y) because a single $z_{1}$ or a
single $y$ gives every voter in $S_{Y}$ at most one approved seat; the
$z$ seat cannot be counted twice for the same voter.

11.text:
For $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ an $\ell$-cohesive set is $|S|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR is $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|
\ge\ell$.

The only $|\bigcap A_{i}|\ge \ell>0$ sets with $|S|\ge 2\ell$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, 
$\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
$S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and for $\ell=3$

\[
\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3 . \tag{X}
\]

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W},z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$.
Then 
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1}$ and (X) is
$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, 
$\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive and with $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2},
\]
so
\[
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2 . \tag{Y}
\]

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  Hence (Y) is
$|W\cap B|\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 3 ,
\]

and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ is strict.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X) and (Y) hold.  $ |W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$,
which makes $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1<2$, so $S_{Y}$ is not
$2$-represented.  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$, violating (Y).  Hence
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

For the lower bound write $t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$.
$a=0$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$, contradicting (X).
$a=1$ forces $u=2$ to obtain $a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$,
i.e. $t\ge3$.  The smallest feasible is $a=2,u=0$, with
$\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$ and $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.

E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is
$2$-represented.  $t=0,1$ is impossible for (X).  Hence

$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and it is attainable.

Thus an EJR $5$-committee satisfies $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ and both
extremes are realised.  This is min $2$ max $3$, option H. ∎

12.text:
The only $\ell$-cohesive sets with a non vacuous intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=|S_{X}|/2=3$,
  $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=|S_{Y}|/2=2$,
  $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
so $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u=:t$.  For $S_{X}$

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|A_{3}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$

and EJR for $S_{X}$ is
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3$.
In particular $a\ge2$ unless $u=2$ and $a+u\ge2$ is necessary.

For $S_{Y}$ let $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+z_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+z_{2}$ and

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

is EJR for $S_{Y}$.  Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ because
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  With $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$.

The bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X) and (Y) hold.  A committee with
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would have $|W\cap B|\le1$ and then
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
give $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$, so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented.
The $z_{1}$ seat can help $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ simultaneously but it
does not remove the need for two distinct $B$-seats for a $2$-approval
of a $Y$-voter.

For the lower side $t=a+u=0,1$ makes
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\le2<3$, so
$S_{X}$ is violated.  $t=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter 2 and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters 4-5.  The same is obtained with $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both attainable.  That is
$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.

6.text:
The only $\ell$-cohesive sets that can be active for $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$
are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u=:t$.
Then  

$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$ and

$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$

is EJR for $S_{X}$.  In particular $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$
and $a=1$ forces $u=2$ for (X), i.e. $t\ge3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ and $t=1,0$
are impossible for (X).

For $S_{Y}$ put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$ , $z_{1},z_{2}\in\{0,1\}$.
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+z_{1}$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=p+z_{2}$ and EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}$.

$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
Hence (Y) forces $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le3$.

The bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.

$t=4$ would require $|W\cap B|\le1$, whence $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$
and (Y) is violated.  E.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=1$ and the $Y$-block is not
$2$-represented.  The $z_{1}$ seat can help the $X$-block and the $Y$-block
at the same time but it is still a $B$-seat, so at least two $B$-seats
are necessary for (Y) and they are disjoint from $A_{1}$.

The lower bound $t=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X) and (Y) hold.  With $a=2,u=0$ the
$3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is witnessed by voter $2$ with the private $y_{2}$
and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is witnessed by voter $4$.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with the lower bound $2$ attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$
and the upper bound $3$ attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
In particular $0,1,4$ approvals for voter $1$ are impossible.

This is min $2$ max $3$, i.e. option H.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the group that the lower bound is settled.

$S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.  Write $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$.  With $a=0$ no member of $S_X$ can reach three approvals and with $a=1$ we would need $y_1,z_3\in W$ for voter 1 to reach three, i.e. $|W\cap A_1|\ge3$.  The cheapest way to satisfy the 3-cohesive requirement without using the private part $\{y_1,z_3\}$ of voter 1 is $a=2$ together with one private candidate for the $8,9,10$ voters, $y_2/y_3$ for voters 2/3, or $z_1$ for 8,9,10.  Those two $x$’s are in $A_1$ and $S_Y$ can be 2-represented with two $y$ seats.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$

gives $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_2|=3$ and $|W_{\min}\cap A_4|=2$.  $1$ approval for voter 1 is impossible, so $\min |W\cap A_1|=2$ is locked.

For the upper side the usual $5-2=3$ bound counts the two seats needed for $S_Y$ as completely disjoint from the seats used for $S_X$.  That double counts the $z$ bridge.  $A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$, so $S_Y$ must be represented inside $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$, but $z_1\in A_4\cap A_5\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is the cheapest seat that can give the $8,9,10$ voters their third approval when $a=2$.  In particular $z_1$ can be used at the same time to give voters $4,5$ their second approval.

Once the $X$ block is witnessed by the three $x$’s themselves we do not need a private third approval for $S_X$ at all: voter 1,2,3 can be the $3$-witness with $a=3$.  Then we can still keep one private $A_1$ candidate and only one net $Y$ seat is needed for $S_Y$, the $z$ seat being shared with the $X$ witness.  That is the effective cost of $S_Y$ is one seat outside $A_1$ once the $z$ overlap is allowed.

Hence we can keep $a=3$ and add one private $A_1$ candidate $y_1$ and one $Y$ seat, e.g. up to symmetry

$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$

which gives $|W\cap A_1|=x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1=4$.  $S_X$ is 3-represented by voters 2,3 or 8,9,10 with the three $x$’s, and the $Y$ requirement is met by the $y_4+z_1$ pair that is available through the shared $z$ use for the $X$ block.  The same effect is obtained with $z_1$ in place of $y_4$, i.e. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$, giving voter 1 four $A_1$ approvals and still 3 approvals for a member of $S_X$ and 2 approvals for a member of $S_Y$.

Five $A_1$ approvals would leave no room for $S_Y$ at all, so $4$ is the largest attainable value.  Together with the settled lower bound we have

$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le 4$,

i.e. min 2 max 4.  The claimed max 3 bound is obtained only by insisting that the two seats counted for $S_Y$ are disjoint from the seats counted for $S_X$; once the $z_1$ overlap is recognised the net outside cost drops from two to one and the $A_1$ content can be pushed to four.

4.text:
The only $\ell$-cohesive sets with a non empty common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
      =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
      =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$.

$S_{Y}$ EJR is
\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2},
\]
hence
\[
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}
\]
so at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
With $|W|=5$
\[
t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-|W\cap B|\le 3 .
\tag{1}
\]

For $S_{X}$
\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+u,\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=a+z_{1},
\end{aligned}
\]
and EJR for $\ell=3$ is
\[
a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge 3 .\tag{X}
\]

$a=0$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$; $a=1$ forces $u=2$ and
$t\ge3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ is necessary and $t=0,1$ contradict (X).  $t=2$
is feasible with $a=2,u=0$, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.

The upper bound (1) is attainable.  With $a=3,u=0$, $p=2$ we can take

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$, whence
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contrary to (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$
and $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented; $z_{1}$ cannot be used simultaneously
as the second approval for $4,5$ and as the private lift for $8,9,10$
when the three $x$’s are kept and $y_{1}$ is added.

Hence under EJR
\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]
the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both realised.  This is
option H, $\min2$, $\max3$.

1.text:
For $n=10,\;k=5$ put $n/k=2$.  Let

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W},z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell_{X}=3$.

\[
|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u,\;|A_{2}\cap W|=a+e_{2},\;|A_{3}\cap W|=a+e_{3},
\;|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1},
\]

so EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3,\tag{X}
\]

and in particular $a+u\ge2$; $a+u=0,1$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{2}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}=3$ so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented,
and the $Y$ requirement is met with the $y$ seat together with the
$z_{1}$ overlap that is normally used to lift $8,9,10$ to three approvals.
The same effect is obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{4}$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$, which gives voter $1$ four
approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ and still $3$-represents $S_{X}$ via

Five $A_{1}$ approvals would leave no room for $S_{Y}$ at all, so $5$ is
impossible. The attainable extremum is therefore $4$.

Hence under EJR
$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le4$,
min $2$ is attainable and max $4$ is attainable, i.e. option A, min 2 max 4.

PUBLIC RESPONSE:

$n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  An $\ell$-cohesive set needs $|S|\ge 2\ell$.
The only non-trivial common intersections are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$ is active.  With $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,

  |W\cap A_{1}|=a+u,\;

  |W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\;
  |W\cap A_{8}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}
  \]
  and EJR for $S_{X}$ is
  \begin{equation}
  a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3 .
  \tag{X}
  \end{equation}

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$ is active.  With $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,

  \[
  |W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+b_{1},\qquad 
  |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+b_{2},
  \]
  and EJR for $S_{Y}$ is
  \begin{equation}
  p+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\ge 2 .
  \tag{Y}
  \end{equation}
  $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$, so the two
  approvals required by (Y) must be taken from $YZ=
  \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

Hence $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$
\[
|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3 .
\tag{1}
\]

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$, so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented,

and with the same $a=2$ we may also use $z_{1}$,

$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\min}'\cap A_{4}|=3$.

18.text:
The two only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  $\ell_{X}=3$ and with
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
EJR for $S_{X}$ is
\begin{equation*}
a+\max\{{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3 . \tag{X}
\end{equation*}

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  $\ell_{Y}=2$ and with
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}$,
EJR for $S_{Y}$ is
\begin{equation*}
p+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge 2 . \tag{Y}
\end{equation*}

Put $t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$ and
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ and
$|W|=5$.  (Y) is $ |W\cap B|\ge 2$, for a $Y$ voter can obtain two
approved seats from $B$ only.  Hence

$|W\cap B|\ge2\;\Longleftrightarrow\;t=5-|W\cap B|\le3$,

so $t\le3$ and $t=3$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$ and then
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular the
committees $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ etc. claimed for a max of
four have
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=|W\cap A_{7}|=1$ and violate
the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ requirement.  Hence $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

From (X) $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and $a=1$ forces
${\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=2$, i.e. $t\ge3$.  Thus $t=0,1$ is impossible
for $S_{X}$.  The smallest feasible value is $a=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}=
{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.  With $a=2$ (X) can be met with ${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ and (Y) can be met with $p=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.  The same
is obtained with $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable.

Consequently for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ being attainable, i.e. min 2 max 3,
option H.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can help the $X$-block and the $Y$-block at
the same time, but it cannot supply two distinct approvals to a $Y$
voter; the $2$-cohesive $Y$-block still needs two members of $B$, so the
two seats taken from $B$ are disjoint from $A_{1}$ and the $3$-upper
bound is tight.

$n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  The only $\ell$-cohesive sets with a non-empty
common intersection are

  $\displaystyle\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$.

For $n=10,k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.
The only $\ell$–cohesive sets with a non–empty common intersection are

\tag{Y}

and therefore $|W\cap B|\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$

public_text.11:
For $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ an $\ell$-cohesive set is $|S|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ and EJR is $\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|
\ge\ell$.

The only $|\bigcap A_{i}|\ge \ell>0$ sets with $|S|\ge 2\ell$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, 
$\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.

\[
\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3 . \tag{X}
\]

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$.

$\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2},
\]
so
\[
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2 . \tag{Y}
\]

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  Hence (Y) is
$|W\cap B|\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 3 ,
\]

and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ is strict.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$, violating (Y).  Hence
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$a=1$ forces $u=2$ to obtain $a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$,
i.e. $t\ge3$.  The smallest feasible is $a=2,u=0$, with
$\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$ and $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
