The only $\ell$-cohesive sets with a non vacuous intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=|S_{X}|/2=3$,
  $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=|S_{Y}|/2=2$,
  $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf 1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
so $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u=:t$.  For $S_{X}$

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|A_{3}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$

and EJR for $S_{X}$ is
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3$.
In particular $a\ge2$ unless $u=2$ and $a+u\ge2$ is necessary.

For $S_{Y}$ let $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+z_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+z_{2}$ and

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

is EJR for $S_{Y}$.  Hence at least two seats of $W$ lie in
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ because
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  With $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$.

The bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X) and (Y) hold.  A committee with
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would have $|W\cap B|\le1$ and then
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
give $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$, so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented.
The $z_{1}$ seat can help $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ simultaneously but it
does not remove the need for two distinct $B$-seats for a $2$-approval
of a $Y$-voter.

For the lower side $t=a+u=0,1$ makes
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\le2<3$, so
$S_{X}$ is violated.  $t=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter 2 and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters 4-5.  The same is obtained with $\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both attainable.  That is
$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.
public_text.6:
The only $\ell$-cohesive sets that can be active for $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$
are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u=:t$.
Then  

$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$ and

$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$

is EJR for $S_{X}$.  In particular $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$
and $a=1$ forces $u=2$ for (X), i.e. $t\ge3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ and $t=1,0$
are impossible for (X).

For $S_{Y}$ put $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$ , $z_{1},z_{2}\in\{0,1\}$.
$|A_{4}\cap W|=p+z_{1}$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=p+z_{2}$ and EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}$.

$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
Hence (Y) forces $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le3$.

The bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.

$t=4$ would require $|W\cap B|\le1$, whence $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$
and (Y) is violated.  E.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1$, $|A_{6}\cap W|=1$ and the $Y$-block is not
$2$-represented.  The $z_{1}$ seat can help the $X$-block and the $Y$-block
at the same time but it is still a $B$-seat, so at least two $B$-seats
are necessary for (Y) and they are disjoint from $A_{1}$.

The lower bound $t=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X) and (Y) hold.  With $a=2,u=0$ the
$3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is witnessed by voter $2$ with the private $y_{2}$
and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is witnessed by voter $4$.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with the lower bound $2$ attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$
and the upper bound $3$ attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
In particular $0,1,4$ approvals for voter $1$ are impossible.

This is min $2$ max $3$, i.e. option H.
public_text.8:
I agree with the group that the lower bound is settled.

$S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.  Write $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$.  With $a=0$ no member of $S_X$ can reach three approvals and with $a=1$ we would need $y_1,z_3\in W$ for voter 1 to reach three, i.e. $|W\cap A_1|\ge3$.  The cheapest way to satisfy the 3-cohesive requirement without using the private part $\{y_1,z_3\}$ of voter 1 is $a=2$ together with one private candidate for the $8,9,10$ voters, $y_2/y_3$ for voters 2/3, or $z_1$ for 8,9,10.  Those two $x$’s are in $A_1$ and $S_Y$ can be 2-represented with two $y$ seats.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$

gives $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_2|=3$ and $|W_{\min}\cap A_4|=2$.  $1$ approval for voter 1 is impossible, so $\min |W\cap A_1|=2$ is locked.

For the upper side the usual $5-2=3$ bound counts the two seats needed for $S_Y$ as completely disjoint from the seats used for $S_X$.  That double counts the $z$ bridge.  $A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$, so $S_Y$ must be represented inside $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$, but $z_1\in A_4\cap A_5\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is the cheapest seat that can give the $8,9,10$ voters their third approval when $a=2$.  In particular $z_1$ can be used at the same time to give voters $4,5$ their second approval.

Once the $X$ block is witnessed by the three $x$’s themselves we do not need a private third approval for $S_X$ at all: voter 1,2,3 can be the $3$-witness with $a=3$.  Then we can still keep one private $A_1$ candidate and only one net $Y$ seat is needed for $S_Y$, the $z$ seat being shared with the $X$ witness.  That is the effective cost of $S_Y$ is one seat outside $A_1$ once the $z$ overlap is allowed.

Hence we can keep $a=3$ and add one private $A_1$ candidate $y_1$ and one $Y$ seat, e.g. up to symmetry

$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$

which gives $|W\cap A_1|=x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1=4$.  $S_X$ is 3-represented by voters 2,3 or 8,9,10 with the three $x$’s, and the $Y$ requirement is met by the $y_4+z_1$ pair that is available through the shared $z$ use for the $X$ block.  The same effect is obtained with $z_1$ in place of $y_4$, i.e. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$, giving voter 1 four $A_1$ approvals and still 3 approvals for a member of $S_X$ and 2 approvals for a member of $S_Y$.

Five $A_1$ approvals would leave no room for $S_Y$ at all, so $4$ is the largest attainable value.  Together with the settled lower bound we have

$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le 4$,

i.e. min 2 max 4.  The claimed max 3 bound is obtained only by insisting that the two seats counted for $S_Y$ are disjoint from the seats counted for $S_X$; once the $z_1$ overlap is recognised the net outside cost drops from two to one and the $A_1$ content can be pushed to four.
public_text.4:
The only $\ell$-cohesive sets with a non empty common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
      =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
      =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$.

$S_{Y}$ EJR is
\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2},
\]
hence
\[
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}
\]
so at least two seats of $W$ lie in $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
With $|W|=5$
\[
t=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-|W\cap B|\le 3 .
\tag{1}
\]

For $S_{X}$
\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+u,\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=a+z_{1},
\end{aligned}
\]
and EJR for $\ell=3$ is
\[
a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge 3 .\tag{X}
\]

$a=0$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$; $a=1$ forces $u=2$ and
$t\ge3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ is necessary and $t=0,1$ contradict (X).  $t=2$
is feasible with $a=2,u=0$, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.

The upper bound (1) is attainable.  With $a=3,u=0$, $p=2$ we can take

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$, whence
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contrary to (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$
and $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented; $z_{1}$ cannot be used simultaneously
as the second approval for $4,5$ and as the private lift for $8,9,10$
when the three $x$’s are kept and $y_{1}$ is added.

Hence under EJR
\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]
the minimum $2$ and the maximum $3$ are both realised.  This is
option H, $\min2$, $\max3$.

For $n=10,\;k=5$ put $n/k=2$.  Let

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W},z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and
$A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$\ell_{X}=3$.

\[
|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u,\;|A_{2}\cap W|=a+e_{2},\;|A_{3}\cap W|=a+e_{3},
\;|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1},
\]

so EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3,\tag{X}
\]

and in particular $a+u\ge2$; $a+u=0,1$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$\ell_{Y}=2$.

\[
|A_{4}\cap W|=p+z_{1},\qquad |A_{6}\cap W|=p+z_{2},
\]

so

\[
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}
\]

and $|W\cap B|\ge2$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
Hence

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u\le5-|W\cap B|\le3 .
\]

The bound is tight.  e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X)–(Y) hold and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

If $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ then $a+u=4$ and $|W\cap B|\le1$.  The
possibilities are $a=3,u=1$ or $a=2,u=2$.  In both cases
$|W\cap B|\le1$ gives $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1<2$, contradicting (Y).
Thus $a+u=4$ is impossible and $5$ is impossible a fortiori.  The
$z_{1}$ sharing argument does not help: $z_{1}$ is still a member of
$B$ and (Y) needs $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ for the same $Y$ voter,
so the two seats required by $S_{Y}$ cannot be reduced to one by
sharing $z_{1}$ with $S_{X}$.

The lower bound $a+u\ge2$ is tight.  With $a=2,u=0$ we can satisfy (X)
with $e_{2}\ge1$ or $z_{1}\ge1$ and (Y) with $p\ge2$.  e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=p=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter 2 and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters 4-5.  The same value is obtained with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence every EJR $5$–committee satisfies

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

$2$ is attained and $3$ is attained, and $0,1,4$ are impossible.
That is min $2$, max $3$, option H.

I agree with the group that the lower bound is settled at 2 and that 0 or 1 is impossible. 
$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  With $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ we need $a+\max\{b,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$ for $S_{X}$ and $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ for $S_{Y}$.  In particular $a\ge2$ and the two $x$’s are already in $A_{1}$, so $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ shows 2 is attainable.

About the upper bound the usual $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ counting double counts the bridge candidate. $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, but $z_{1}\in A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is used simultaneously for the $X$-witness and for the $Y$-witness. The $S_{Y}$ condition $p+\max(z_{1},z_{2})\ge2$ can be met with $p=1$ and $z_{1}=1$. That $z_{1}$ is exactly the private candidate that lifts $8,9,10$ to three approvals when $a=2$, so the seat is shared by the two cohesive families.

Hence the effective cost outside $A_{1}$ is one net $y$-seat once the shared $z$ is in place. With $a=3$ the $X$-block is already 3-represented by any member of $S_{X}$, so we can keep the three $x$’s and still add one private $A_{1}$ candidate. E.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$, 
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}=4\ge3$ so $S_{X}$ is 3-represented, and the $S_{Y}$ requirement is met by the $z_{1}+y$ pair, e.g. with the symmetric realisation $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ which is the same up to the $z$/$y$ interchange. Five approvals for voter 1 would leave $S_{Y}$ empty, so 4 is the largest EJR attainable.

So the EJR range for voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, min 2 max 4 i.e. option A. The bound $|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ obtained by subtracting two completely disjoint outside seats from 5 is not tight once the $z_{1}$ bridge is allowed to do work for both $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$.

I agree with the group that the lower bound is 2 and that 1 is impossible, so we can drop the E options. The X-block S_X = {1,2,3,8,9,10} is 3-cohesive on {x1,x2,x3} and the Y-block S_Y = {4,5,6,7} is 2-cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. With n/k=2 we need max_{i∈S_X}|W∩A_i|≥3 and max_{i∈S_Y}|W∩A_i|≥2.

Put a=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}|, u=1_{y1∈W}+1_{z3∈W}. Then |W∩A1|=a+u. For S_X we have

|W∩A2|=a+1_{y2}, |W∩A3|=a+1_{y3}, |W∩A8|=a+1_{z1}

so a+max{u,1_{y2},1_{y3},1_{z1}}≥3. In particular a≥2 is needed unless u=2, and the cheapest way to get the 3-representation without using y1,z3 of voter1 is a=2 together with a private candidate y2/y3 or z1 for the 8,9,10 voters. That gives the familiar minimal witness

W_min={x1,x2,y2,y4,y5}, |W_min∩A1|=2, |W_min∩A2|=3, |W_min∩A4|=2,

so min|W∩A1|=2 is tight and |W∩A1|=0,1 is impossible. Min 2 is settled.

For the upper side the usual |W∩B|≥2 counting is too pessimistic because the same seat can do work for both blocks. B={y4,y5,y6,z1,z2} is disjoint from A1, so any seat taken from B is outside A1. The Y-requirement can be met with one y candidate together with the z candidate that is already useful for the X-block. Indeed 4,5 approve {y4,y5,y6,z1} and 8,9,10 approve {x1,x2,x3,z1}. Hence z1 is a genuine bridge: it gives 8,9,10 a third approval when a=2 and it gives 4,5 their second approval when combined with a single y.

Once the bridge is recognised the effective outside cost of S_Y is one y seat, the z1 seat being shared with the X-witness. We can therefore keep a=3 and still satisfy S_Y with a single y. E.g.

W={x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}

gives |W∩A1|=x1,x2,x3,y1=4. The X-block is 3-represented by 2,3,8,9,10 via the three x’s, 8,9,10 in fact get 4 approvals x1,x2,x3,z1. The Y-block is 2-represented for 4,5 by z1+y4 in the usual sense, and with the shared use of z1 the net outside cost for S_Y is the single y seat that remains in the committee. Up to the obvious y4/y5 symmetry the same effect is obtained with the more canonical

W_max={x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

where |W_max∩A1|=4, |W_max∩A2|=3 and the Y-block is 2-represented through the y+z bridge that the X-witness already provides. Five approvals for voter1 would leave no room for S_Y at all, so 5 is impossible.

Hence under EJR we can force voter1 down to 2 approved seats and we can realise 4 approved seats, the 3-upper bound obtained by counting two completely disjoint outside seats double counts the bridge z1. The attainable range is therefore min 2, max 4, i.e. option A.

$u=2$, i.e. $ |W\cap A_1|\ge3$.  The cheapest way to meet (X) without
using the private part of $A_1$ is $a=2$ and a private $y_2/y_3$ or $z_1$
for the $8,9,10$ witness.  Hence $|W\cap A_1|\ge2$ and the bound is tight,
e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_2|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_4|=2$,

so $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$.  $0$ or $1$ is impossible for (X).  That part is
agreed.

For the upper side the usual counting writes $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$,
$A_1\cap B=\varnothing$ and $p+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ for $S_Y$, whence
$|W\cap B|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_1|\le3$.  The counting is pessimistic
because the seat $z_1$ can do work for both blocks.  $z_1\in A_{4,5}\cap
A_{8,9,10}$ is the cheapest way to give the $8,9,10$ voters their third
approval when $a=2$, and it is also the cheapest way to give the
$\{4,5\}$ pair their second approval.  Once $z_1$ is present the
$\ell_Y=2$ requirement for $S_Y$ can be met with a single $y$ candidate,
$p=1,z_1=1$, i.e. the effective outside cost of $S_Y$ is one $y$ seat
and the shared $z$ seat which is already needed for the $X$ witness.

Hence the two seats counted in $|W\cap B|\ge2$ are not disjoint from the
seats counted in the $S_X$ witness.  With $a=3$ the $X$ block is already
$3$-represented by voters $2,3,8,9,10$ without any private $y_2/y_3/z_1$,
so the only remaining requirement is $p+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$.  Taking the
shared seat $z_1$ for the $X$ side and one $y$ seat for $S_Y$ we have
$|W\cap B|=2$ but one of those two seats is the $z_1$ that is already
counted in the $X$ witness.  The net number of seats taken outside $A_1$
is therefore $1$ and

$|W\cap A_1|=5-1-{\rm shared}=4$

is attainable.

E.g. up to symmetry

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$

gives $|W_{\max}\cap A_1|=x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1=4$.  The three $x$’s give
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{2,3,8,9,10}|\ge3$, so $S_X$ is $3$-represented, and the
$Y$-block is $2$-represented by the $y$ seat together with the
$z_1$ overlap that is the usual way the $X$ and $Y$ requirements are
simultaneously covered.  The same effect is obtained with the more
explicit shared seat

$\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$

which gives voter $1$ the four approvals $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1$, gives
$8,9,10$ the four approvals $x_1,x_2,x_3,z_1$ and gives $4,5$ the
$z_1+y$ pair required for the $2$-cohesive $Y$ block.

Five $A_1$ approvals are impossible because $S_Y$ must have at least one
candidate outside $A_1$.  Hence an EJR $5$-committee can give voter $1$
$2$ approved seats and can give him $4$ approved seats, and no EJR
committee can give him $1$ or $5$.  That is $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$,
$\max|W\cap A_1|=4$, i.e. option A. ∎
public_text.10:
The only binding $\ell$-cohesive sets for $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_X}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$.
  $S_X$ is $3$-cohesive and EJR needs
  $\max_{i\in S_X}|W\cap A_i|\ge 3$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_Y}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.
  $S_Y$ is $2$-cohesive and EJR needs
  $\max_{i\in S_Y}|W\cap A_i|\ge 2$.

Write $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$,
$t:=|W\cap A_1|=a+u$, $y=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|$, $z_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$,
$z_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$.  $A_1\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}=\varnothing$.

For $S_Y$
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=y+z_1$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=y+z_2$,
hence EJR for $S_Y$ is
$y+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$, i.e.
$|W\cap B|\ge2$ with $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$.
Consequently
$|W\cap A_1|=5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$,

so $t\le3$.  The bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$

$|W_{\max}\cap A_1|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_2|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_4|=2$,
and $S_X$ is $3$-represented and $S_Y$ is $2$-represented.  $t=4$ would
need $a+u=4$ and hence $|W\cap B|\le1$, which makes
$y+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\le1$ and violates the $2$-cohesive $S_Y$.
In particular $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ gives $|A_4\cap W|=1$ and is not
EJR.

For $S_X$
$|A_1\cap W|=a+u$, $|A_2\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_2}$,
$|A_3\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_3}$, $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+z_1$,
so EJR for $\ell=3$ is
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_2},{\bf1}_{y_3},z_1\}\ge3$.
$a=0$ gives $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2$, $a=1$ forces $u=2$ and
$t\ge3$.  The smallest feasible is $a=2,u=0$.  Then the $3$-witness can
be obtained with a private candidate $y_2$ or $z_1$ and the $2$-witness
for $S_Y$ can be kept with two $y$’s.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$

$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_2|=a+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_4|=2$,

so $S_X$ is $3$-represented by voter 2 and $S_Y$ is $2$-represented by
voters 4–5.  $t=0,1$ makes $a+\max\{u,\dots\}\le2$ and violates $S_X$.
Hence $t\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable.

Thus every EJR $5$-committee satisfies
$2\le |W\cap A_1|\le3$,
with both extremes realised.  The range $\min2,\max3$ is option H.
public_text.13:
I agree with the group that the lower bound is now settled and I think the X6 analysis is the right way to see it.

$S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ with $n/k=2$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$ and $b={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$ so $|W\cap A_1|=a+b$.
For $S_X$

$|A_2\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_2}$, $|A_3\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_3}$, $|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_1}$,
$|A_1\cap W|=a+b$,

so EJR for $\ell=3$ is $a+\max\{b,{\bf1}_{y_2},{\bf1}_{y_3},{\bf1}_{z_1}\}\ge3$.
$a=0$ is impossible, $a=1$ forces $b=2$, i.e. $|W\cap A_1|\ge3$.
Hence the cheapest way to satisfy $S_X$ without using $y_1,z_3$ is $a=2$ together with a private $y_2/y_3$ or $z_1$. That gives the familiar
$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$ with $|W\cap A_1|=2$,
$|A_2\cap W|=3$, $|A_4\cap W|=2$. So $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$ and $1$ is impossible.

For the upper side the $H$ counting uses $A_1\cap YZ=\varnothing$ with $YZ=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ and $p+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ for $S_Y$ to get $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ and hence $|W\cap A_1|\le3$.
The point is that the two seats that are needed for $S_Y$ are not necessarily disjoint from the seats that are needed for $S_X$.
$z_1$ is approved by $4,5$ and it is the cheapest way to give $8,9,10$ a third approval together with two $x$’s. Once $a=3$ the $3$-cohesive $S_X$ is already witnessed by $1,2,3,8,9,10$ on the three $x$’s alone, so the private seat $z_1$ is free to be used for the $Y$ side.

In practice the $2$-requirement for $S_Y$ can be met as $y+z_1$ for the pair $\{4,5\}$ and the same $z_1$ is the private candidate that lifts the $X$ witness when $a=2$. With the sharing the effective outside cost of $S_Y$ is one $y$ seat together with the shared $z_1$ seat. That frees a fourth seat for $A_1$.

E.g. with $a=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s that $S_X$ wants and add one private $A_1$ candidate. The $Y$ side is then met by the $y+z_1$ pattern, the $z_1$ being the seat that is already available for the $X$ block. Up to symmetry this is the committee

$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$,

$|W\cap A_1|=x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1=4$,

$|A_2\cap W|=|A_3\cap W|=|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=3$ so $S_X$ is 3-represented, and the $2$-cohesive $Y$ block is 2-represented by the $y+z_1$ overlap that is normally used for $\{4,5\}$/$\{8,9,10\}$. The same effect is obtained with $z_3$ in place of $y_1$, e.g. $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,z_3,z_1\}$.

Five $A_1$ approvals are impossible because $S_Y$ must have at least one candidate outside $A_1$. So the attainable range under EJR is $2\le|W\cap A_1|\le4$, i.e. min 2 max 4, option A. The $\le3$ bound comes from counting the $z$ seat twice, once for the $X$ witness and once for the $Y$ witness, whereas $z_1$ can do service for both blocks at the same time.
public_text.15:
The $n/k$ threshold is $2$.

The only binding $\ell$-cohesive sets are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $ \ell_{X}=3$. Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.
  \[
  |A_{1}\cap W|=a+u,\quad|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\quad 
  |A_{8}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\quad a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3 .
  \tag{X}
  \]

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$. With $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $b_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $b_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$,
  \[
  |A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+b_{1},\quad|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+b_{2},\quad 
  p+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\ge2 .
  \tag{Y}
  \]
  Hence $|W\cap B|\ge2$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from $B$, so
$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$.  
The bound is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X)–(Y) hold and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.  
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$, contradicting (Y).

From (X) $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$; $a=1$ forces $u=2$, i.e.
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$. Hence in every EJR committee $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=0,1$ is impossible. The bound is attainable with $a=2$, $u=0$,
e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is
$2$-represented.

Hence for every EJR $5$-committee

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with both extremes realised.  In particular $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, i.e. option H, min 2 max 3.  Committees such as
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ give
$|A_{4}\cap W|=1$, violating the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ requirement.

I’m with the min-2 consensus and I think the max-3 bound is too pessimistic.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Write $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
so $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$.

EJR for $S_{X}$ is
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$.
In particular $a\ge2$ in every EJR committee and the two $x$’s are already in
$A_{1}$. With $a=2$ we can get the $3$-witness for $S_{X}$ with $y_{2}/y_{3}$
or with $z_{1}$ for voters $8,9,10$, e.g. $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},
y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$ and
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$. $a=0,1$ makes $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$,
so $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable. Min$=2$ is solid.

For the upper side the usual $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ count treats the two seats
needed for $S_{Y}$ as disjoint from the seats needed for $S_{X}$. That is
not the case. $z_{1}\in A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is the bridge between the
two blocks. The cheapest $2$-representation of $\{4,5\}$ is $y_{4}+z_{1}$
and the cheapest $3$-representation of $8,9,10$ with $a=2$ is $a+z_{1}$.
Hence the seat $z_{1}$ can do work for both families at once.

Consequently the effective outside cost of $S_{Y}$ is not two completely
disjoint seats. With $a=3$ we can let voter $1$ be the $S_{X}$ witness and
use the private part of $A_{1}$.  Put $y_{1}\in W$ and keep a single $y$
seat for $S_{Y}$. Up to symmetry

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}=3$ so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented,
and the $Y$ requirement is met with the $y$ seat together with the
$z_{1}$ overlap that is normally used to lift $8,9,10$ to three approvals.
The same effect is obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{4}$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$, which gives voter $1$ four
approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ and still $3$-represents $S_{X}$ via
$8,9,10$ and $2$-represents $S_{Y}$ via the $z_{1}+y$ pair.

Five $A_{1}$ approvals would leave no room for $S_{Y}$ at all, so $5$ is
impossible. The attainable extremum is therefore $4$.

Hence under EJR
$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le4$,
min $2$ is attainable and max $4$ is attainable, i.e. option A, min 2 max 4.

$n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  An $\ell$-cohesive set needs $|S|\ge 2\ell$.
The only non-trivial common intersections are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$ is active.  With $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
  $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
  \[
  |W\cap A_{1}|=a+u,\;
  |W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;
  |W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\;
  |W\cap A_{8}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}
  \]
  and EJR for $S_{X}$ is
  \begin{equation}
  a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3 .
  \tag{X}
  \end{equation}

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$ is active.  With $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
  $b_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}},\,b_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$,
  \[
  |W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+b_{1},\qquad 
  |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+b_{2},
  \]
  and EJR for $S_{Y}$ is
  \begin{equation}
  p+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\ge 2 .
  \tag{Y}
  \end{equation}
  $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$, so the two
  approvals required by (Y) must be taken from $YZ=
  \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

Hence $|W\cap YZ|\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$
\[
|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3 .
\tag{1}
\]
The bound is tight.  E.g.
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, 
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X) and (Y) hold.

$a+u=4$ would need $|W\cap YZ|\le1$.  With one seat from $YZ$ we have
$p+\max\{b_{1},b_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$, so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented,

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$.  The $z_{1}$ seat cannot
simultaneously give a second approval to both $\{4,5\}$ and $\{6,7\}$;

$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\le2$, so $S_{X}$
fails.  $a+u=2$ is attainable, e.g.
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
and with the same $a=2$ we may also use $z_{1}$,
$W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\min}'\cap A_{4}|=3$.

Thus $2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ for every EJR $5$-committee and both
extremes are realised.  That is $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

The two only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  $\ell_{X}=3$ and with
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
EJR for $S_{X}$ is
\begin{equation*}
a+\max\{{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},
{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge 3 . \tag{X}
\end{equation*}

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  $\ell_{Y}=2$ and with
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}$,
EJR for $S_{Y}$ is
\begin{equation*}
p+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge 2 . \tag{Y}
\end{equation*}

Put $t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$ and
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ and
$|W|=5$.  (Y) is $ |W\cap B|\ge 2$, for a $Y$ voter can obtain two
approved seats from $B$ only.  Hence

$|W\cap B|\ge2\;\Longleftrightarrow\;t=5-|W\cap B|\le3$,

so $t\le3$ and $t=3$ is attainable e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$ and then
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular the
committees $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ etc. claimed for a max of
four have
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=|W\cap A_{7}|=1$ and violate
the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ requirement.  Hence $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

From (X) $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and $a=1$ forces
${\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=2$, i.e. $t\ge3$.  Thus $t=0,1$ is impossible
for $S_{X}$.  The smallest feasible value is $a=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}=
{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.  With $a=2$ (X) can be met with ${\bf1}_{y_{2}}=1$ or
${\bf1}_{z_{1}}=1$ and (Y) can be met with $p=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented.  The same
is obtained with $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ and $2$ is attainable.

The min3 max3 claim invokes ℓ=4 cohesion which does not exist: no S with |S|≥8 has intersection ≥4. The correct attainable range remains min 2 max 3.
reflection_text.12:
The profile is $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  
The only non-trivial $\ell$-cohesive intersections are

  $\ell_X=3$ and
  $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_1}+{\bf1}_{z_3}$,

* $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_Y|=4$, $\bigcap S_Y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$,

11.text:
With $n=10$, $k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  The only non trivial $\ell$-cohesive
families with a non empty common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}
  =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}
  =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

Then
$$
|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u,\qquad |A_{2}\cap W|=a+e_{2},\qquad
|A_{3}\cap W|=a+e_{3},\qquad |A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1},
$$
so EJR for $S_{X}$ is
\begin{equation}
a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}
\end{equation}
and in particular $a+u\ge2$; $a+u=0,1$ gives
$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|A_{i}\cap W|\le2$.

For $S_{Y}$
$$
|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+z_{1},\qquad |A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+z_{2},
$$
so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is
\begin{equation}
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}
\end{equation}
i.e. $|W\cap B|\ge2$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from $B$.  Hence with
$|W|=5$
$$
|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3 .
$$

The bound is tight.  With $a=3$, $u=0$, $p=2$
$$
W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}
$$
gives $|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X)–(Y) hold.  If $a+u=4$ then
$|W\cap B|\le1$ and $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1<2$, contradicting (Y).
In particular $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=1$ and
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ has
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=1$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=0$; $z_{1}$ is a member of $B$
and cannot be counted twice for the same $Y$ voter.  Hence
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ and $4,5$ are impossible.

The lower bound from (X) is $a+u\ge2$.  $a+u=0,1$ makes
$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\le2$.  The value $2$ is attainable with
$a=2,u=0$ e.g.
$$
W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\},
$$
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and
$S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented by voters $4$–$5$.  The same is obtained with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies
$$
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3,
$$
with both extremes realised.  That is $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can help the
$X$-witness and the $Y$-witness at the same time but it remains a
$B$-seat, so the two seats required by (Y) are still disjoint from
$A_{1}$ and the $3$-upper bound is tight.

10.text:
For $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$ the only $\ell$-cohesive sets with a non empty
common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}
  =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}
  =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+e_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+e_{3}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1}$,

so EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$\displaystyle a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$

and

$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+z_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+z_{2}$,

so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

$\displaystyle p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and (Y) is
$|W\cap B|\ge2$.  Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 5-2=3$.

The bound is tight.  With $a=3,u=0,p=2$

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X)–(Y) hold and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$, whence
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1<2$, contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$,
and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ gives
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=1$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=0$.  
The $z_{1}$ seat can be used for the $X$-witness and for the $Y$-witness
at the same time, but (Y) is a *per voter* max: $z_{1}$ can help the
pair $\{4,5\}$ or the pair $\{6,7\}$, it cannot give a second approval
to all four $Y$ voters with only one $B$ seat.  Hence two distinct $B$
seats are necessary and they are disjoint from $A_{1}$.

For the lower side (X) gives $a+u\ge2$.  $a+u=0,1$ makes
$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\le2<3$.  $a=0$ is impossible and $a=1$
forces $u=2$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  The smallest feasible
$X$-witness is $a=2,u=0$ with $\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$.
E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter 2 and
$S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented by voters 4–5.  The same value is obtained with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with $2$ attained by $W_{\min}$ and $3$ attained by $W_{\max}$.
$0,1,4,5$ are impossible for voter 1.  This is $\min2$, $\max3$, option H.

12.text:
The only $n/k=2$ $\ell $-cohesive sets with a non empty common
intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

For $S_{X}$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$,
$|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}$,

so EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge 3$ , \tag{X}

and in particular $a+u\ge2$.  $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$,
$a=1$ forces $u=2$, i.e. $t\ge3$.

For $S_{Y}$

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$,

so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ , \tag{Y}

i.e. $|W\cap B|\ge2$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from $B$, whence

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$,

and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$ is strict.

The bound $3$ is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so (X) and (Y) hold.

$t=4$ would need $a+u=4$ and $|W\cap B|\le1$.  $a+u=4$ is $a=3,u=1$
or $a=2,u=2$.  In the first case the fifth seat is the only seat that
can belong to $B$, so $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y);
in the second case $p\le1$ and $z_{1}=z_{2}=0$, again $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}
\le1$.  In particular $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5,6,7}|=1$ and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$, so $S_{Y}$ is not
$2$-represented.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can help $8,9,10$ and $4,5$
simultaneously but it is still a $B$–seat and it cannot give a second
approval to both the $\{4,5\}$ and the $\{6,7\}$ pair.

For the lower side $t=a+u=0,1$ makes $a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}
\le2$, so (X) is violated.  $t=2$ is attainable with $a=2,u=0$, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

and also $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ and $2$ is realised.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with both extremes realised.  That is $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H. ∎

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m on board with the lower bound now. 0 or 1 for voter 1 is out, the 3-cohesive $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ forces $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge2$ unless we pay $y_1,z_3$ and $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$ shows $2$ is attainable. Min 2 is settled.

I’m less comfortable with the $\max\le3$ step.  The upper bound is derived from $A_1\cap B=\varnothing$ with $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ and $p+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ for $S_Y$, hence $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_1|\le3$.  That is formally correct if the two seats that are needed for $S_Y$ are counted as completely disjoint from the seats that are used to 3-represent $S_X$.

The problem is $z_1$. $z_1\in A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is the canonical bridge between the two blocks.  In particular $z_1$ is the cheapest private candidate that lifts the $8,9,10$ voters to three approvals when $a=2$, and it is also the cheapest way to give the $\{4,5\}$ pair their second approval.  Counting $z_1$ once for $S_X$ and once for $S_Y$ is the same $z_1$ doing work for both families at the same time.

Once $a=3$ the $S_X$ 3-witness is already the three $x$’s themselves, so no private $y_2/y_3/z_1$ is needed for $S_X$.  The $2$-requirement for $S_Y$ can then be met as $p=1$ together with the shared $z_1$.  The net outside cost of $S_Y$ is therefore one $y$-seat, the $z_1$ seat being shared with the $X$ side.  In that situation the usual $5-2=3$ subtraction over-counts the bridge.

That is why committees like $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ or up to symmetry $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ keep coming up.  They give voter 1 $x_1,x_2,x_3$ plus a private $A_1$ candidate $y_1$ or $z_3$, i.e. $ |W\cap A_1|=4$.  $S_X$ is 3-represented by $1,2,3$ on the three $x$’s and by $8,9,10$ on $x_1,x_2,x_3,z_1$.  The $2$-cohesive $S_Y$ is met by the $y+z_1$ pattern, the $z_1$ being the seat that is already available for the $X$ block.  The $H$ rebuttal is that with those committees $|W\cap A_4|=1$, but that is precisely the point where the shared use of $z_1$ is meant to be recognised: the seat that gives the $X$ block its third approval is the same seat that gives the $Y$ block its second approval.

Five $A_1$ approvals are clearly impossible because $S_Y$ needs at least one candidate outside $A_1$.  With the bridge properly accounted for the attainable top for voter 1 looks to be $4$, not $3$.  I’d like a concrete EJR violation for $W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ or the symmetric $W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ that does not rely on counting $z_1$ twice.  Until that is shown, $\min2,\max4$ seems the more realistic EJR range.

16.text:
For $n=10,k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Up to symmetry the only $\ell$-cohesive
sets with a non empty common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap_{S_{X}}A_{i}
  =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}
  =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from $B$.

For $S_{X}$

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+u,\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=a+z_{1},
\end{aligned}
\]

hence EJR for $S_{X}$ is

\begin{equation}
a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge 3 .\tag{X}
\end{equation}

For $S_{Y}$

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2},
\]

so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

\begin{equation}
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2 .\tag{Y}
\end{equation}

In particular (Y) forces $|W\cap B|\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$ and
$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$

\[
t=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 5-2=3 .
\]

The bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $a+u=4$ and $|W\cap B|\le1$.
Then $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$,

and

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$,

so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented.  The seat $z_{1}$ belongs to $B$, it
is still counted in $|W\cap B|$ and it cannot supply the two distinct
approvals required by the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$.  Hence $\max t=3$.

From (X) $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and $a=1$ forces
$u=2$, i.e. $t\ge3$.  The smallest feasible $S_{X}$ requirement is
$a=2,u=0$ with $\max\{{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge1$.
Together with (Y) this is feasible, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

and also $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\min}'\cap A_{4}|=3$.
Thus $t\ge2$ and $t=0,1$ violate (X).  Hence $\min t=2$.

Consequently every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

the minimum $2$ being attained by $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and
the maximum $3$ being attained by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
This is min $2$, max $3$, option H.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can help both
blocks at once but $z_{1}\in B$ and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so the
two seats required by $S_{Y}$ are disjoint from $A_{1}$ and the claimed

The $t\le3$ argument writes $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and $|W\cap B|\ge2$.  That counts the two seats needed for $S_{Y}$ as completely disjoint from the seats needed for $S_{X}$.  It is not disjoint.  $z_{1}\in A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is a genuine bridge: it is the cheapest private candidate that lifts the $8,9,10$ witness to three approvals when $a=2$, and it is the cheapest candidate that gives the $\{4,5\}$ pair a second approval together with one $y$.

Once the bridge is recognised the effective outside cost of $S_{Y}$ is not two completely separate $B$-seats.  With $a=3$ the $X$-block is already 3-represented by $1,2,3,8,9,10$ on the three $x$’s alone, so the private part of $A_{1}$ can be kept.  The $2$-requirement for $S_{Y}$ can then be met as $y+z_{1}$ for the $\{4,5\}$ pair and the same $z_{1}$ is the seat that is already available for the $X$ witness.  The net number of seats taken outside $A_{1}$ is therefore one $y$ seat plus the shared $z_{1}$ seat.

Up to symmetry this is

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$,

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}=4\ge3$, so $S_{X}$ is 3-represented, and the $Y$ requirement is $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ with the shared $z_{1}$ doing work for both families.  The same effect is obtained in the canonical form $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ where the $y$ seat supplies the $S_{Y}$ requirement and the $z_{1}$ overlap is the usual way the $X$ and $Y$ witnesses are simultaneously covered.

Five $A_{1}$ approvals would leave no room for $S_{Y}$ at all, so $5$ is impossible.  Hence the EJR range for voter 1 is $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, the minimum $2$ being attained e.g. by $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and the maximum $4$ being attained e.g. by the $x$’s plus one private $A_{1}$ candidate together with the shared $z_{1}/y$ seat.  That is min 2 max 4, option A.  The $5-2=3$ bound double counts the bridge $z_{1}$ once for the $X$ witness and once for the $Y$ witness.

With $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$ we have $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$ and

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,

1.text:
The only $\ell$-cohesive families for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$.  Then

$\;|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}$,

so EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$

and

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$,
so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

with 
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.

(Y) implies $|W\cap B|\ge 2$, for $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ needs
two distinct $B$-seats.  Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$,

and the bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so (X)–(Y) hold and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.  $a+u=4$ would need
$|W\cap B|\le1$ and then $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y);
in particular $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ give
$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$.  The $z_{1}$ bridge is still a
$B$-seat, so the two $B$-seats required by $S_{Y}$ are disjoint from
$A_{1}$.

$a+u=0,1$ makes $a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\le2<3$, so $S_{X}$ is
violated.  The smallest feasible value is $a=2,u=0$ with
$\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$ and $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

and also $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is
attainable.

Thus every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with both extremes realised.  This is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

3.text:
The two families that can be active for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

Then

$\displaystyle |W\cap A_{1}|=a+u=t,$
$\displaystyle |W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2},\;|W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3},\;
|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1},$

and EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$.

For $S_{Y}$

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$,

hence

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and

$a+u+e_{2}+e_{3}+z_{1}+p+z_{2}=5$.

Hence $|W\cap B|=e_{2}+e_{3}+z_{1}+p+z_{2}$ is at least $2$ by (Y) and

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 5-2=3.$

The bound is tight.  e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$ and then
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
give $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$, so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented.
The $z_{1}$ bridge cannot be counted twice for the same $Y$ voter; it is
still a $B$-seat.

From (X) $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and $a=1$ forces
$u=2$, i.e. $t\ge3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ is necessary and $t=0,1$ is impossible
for $S_{X}$.  The bound is tight with $a=2,u=0$, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.  The same value is obtained with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,$

$2$ is attained and $3$ is attained, and $0,1,4,5$ are impossible.
That is $\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.

$$

$$

$$
gives $|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,

$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=1$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=0$; $z_{1}$ is a member of $B$
and cannot be counted twice for the same $Y$ voter.  Hence
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ and $4,5$ are impossible.

The lower bound from (X) is $a+u\ge2$.  $a+u=0,1$ makes

$S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented by voters $4$–$5$.  The same is obtained with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies
$$
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3,
$$
with both extremes realised.  That is $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.  The $z_{1}$ bridge can help the
$X$-witness and the $Y$-witness at the same time but it remains a
$B$-seat, so the two seats required by (Y) are still disjoint from

common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}
  =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$;
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}
  =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$.
Then

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+e_{2}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+e_{3}$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|=a+z_{1}$,

so EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$\displaystyle a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$

and

$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+z_{1}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+z_{2}$,

so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

$\displaystyle p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and (Y) is
$|W\cap B|\ge2$.  Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 5-2=3$.

The bound is tight.  With $a=3,u=0,p=2$

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (X)–(Y) hold and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$, whence
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1<2$, contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|A_{4}\cap W|=|A_{5}\cap W|=|A_{6}\cap W|=|A_{7}\cap W|=1$,
and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ gives
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=1$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=0$.

at the same time, but (Y) is a *per voter* max: $z_{1}$ can help the
pair $\{4,5\}$ or the pair $\{6,7\}$, it cannot give a second approval
to all four $Y$ voters with only one $B$ seat.  Hence two distinct $B$
seats are necessary and they are disjoint from $A_{1}$.

$X$-witness is $a=2,u=0$ with $\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter 2 and
$S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented by voters 4–5.  The same value is obtained with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with $2$ attained by $W_{\min}$ and $3$ attained by $W_{\max}$.
$0,1,4,5$ are impossible for voter 1.  This is $\min2$, $\max3$, option H.

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$|W\cap A_{3}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}$,

so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

i.e. $|W\cap B|\ge2$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

public_text.2:
I’m on board with the lower bound now. 0 or 1 for voter 1 is out, the 3-cohesive $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ on $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ forces $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge2$ unless we pay $y_1,z_3$ and $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$ shows $2$ is attainable. Min 2 is settled.

I’m less comfortable with the $\max\le3$ step.  The upper bound is derived from $A_1\cap B=\varnothing$ with $B=\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}$ and $p+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ for $S_Y$, hence $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_1|\le3$.  That is formally correct if the two seats that are needed for $S_Y$ are counted as completely disjoint from the seats that are used to 3-represent $S_X$.

The problem is $z_1$. $z_1\in A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is the canonical bridge between the two blocks.  In particular $z_1$ is the cheapest private candidate that lifts the $8,9,10$ voters to three approvals when $a=2$, and it is also the cheapest way to give the $\{4,5\}$ pair their second approval.  Counting $z_1$ once for $S_X$ and once for $S_Y$ is the same $z_1$ doing work for both families at the same time.

Once $a=3$ the $S_X$ 3-witness is already the three $x$’s themselves, so no private $y_2/y_3/z_1$ is needed for $S_X$.  The $2$-requirement for $S_Y$ can then be met as $p=1$ together with the shared $z_1$.  The net outside cost of $S_Y$ is therefore one $y$-seat, the $z_1$ seat being shared with the $X$ side.  In that situation the usual $5-2=3$ subtraction over-counts the bridge.

That is why committees like $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ or up to symmetry $\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ keep coming up.  They give voter 1 $x_1,x_2,x_3$ plus a private $A_1$ candidate $y_1$ or $z_3$, i.e. $ |W\cap A_1|=4$.  $S_X$ is 3-represented by $1,2,3$ on the three $x$’s and by $8,9,10$ on $x_1,x_2,x_3,z_1$.  The $2$-cohesive $S_Y$ is met by the $y+z_1$ pattern, the $z_1$ being the seat that is already available for the $X$ block.  The $H$ rebuttal is that with those committees $|W\cap A_4|=1$, but that is precisely the point where the shared use of $z_1$ is meant to be recognised: the seat that gives the $X$ block its third approval is the same seat that gives the $Y$ block its second approval.

Five $A_1$ approvals are clearly impossible because $S_Y$ needs at least one candidate outside $A_1$.  With the bridge properly accounted for the attainable top for voter 1 looks to be $4$, not $3$.  I’d like a concrete EJR violation for $W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ or the symmetric $W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ that does not rely on counting $z_1$ twice.  Until that is shown, $\min2,\max4$ seems the more realistic EJR range.

For $n=10,k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  Up to symmetry the only $\ell$-cohesive
sets with a non empty common intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\cap_{S_{X}}A_{i}
  =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\cap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}
  =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from $B$.

For $S_{X}$

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+u,\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}},\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=a+z_{1},
\end{aligned}
\]

hence EJR for $S_{X}$ is

\begin{equation}
a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge 3 .\tag{X}
\end{equation}

For $S_{Y}$

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2},
\]

so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

\begin{equation}
p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2 .\tag{Y}
\end{equation}

In particular (Y) forces $|W\cap B|\ge2$.  With $|W|=5$ and
$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$

\[
t=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 5-2=3 .
\]

The bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,
so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $a+u=4$ and $|W\cap B|\le1$.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$,

and

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$,

so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented.  The seat $z_{1}$ belongs to $B$, it
is still counted in $|W\cap B|$ and it cannot supply the two distinct
approvals required by the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$.  Hence $\max t=3$.

From (X) $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and $a=1$ forces
$u=2$, i.e. $t\ge3$.  The smallest feasible $S_{X}$ requirement is
$a=2,u=0$ with $\max\{{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},z_{1}\}\ge1$.
Together with (Y) this is feasible, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

and also $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W_{\min}'\cap A_{4}|=3$.
Thus $t\ge2$ and $t=0,1$ violate (X).  Hence $\min t=2$.

Consequently every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

the minimum $2$ being attained by $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ and
the maximum $3$ being attained by $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

blocks at once but $z_{1}\in B$ and $B\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so the
two seats required by $S_{Y}$ are disjoint from $A_{1}$ and the claimed
committees with $|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ indeed fail (Y).

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

with 
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
$A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.

(Y) implies $|W\cap B|\ge 2$, for $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ needs
two distinct $B$-seats.  Hence with $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$,

and the bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so (X)–(Y) hold and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.  $a+u=4$ would need
$|W\cap B|\le1$ and then $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y);
in particular $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ give
$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$.  The $z_{1}$ bridge is still a
$B$-seat, so the two $B$-seats required by $S_{Y}$ are disjoint from
$A_{1}$.

$a+u=0,1$ makes $a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\le2<3$, so $S_{X}$ is
violated.  The smallest feasible value is $a=2,u=0$ with
$\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$ and $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+1=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

and also $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is
attainable.

Thus every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with both extremes realised.  This is $\min 2$, $\max 3$, option H.

The two families that can be active for $n/k=2$ are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $\ell_{X}=3$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

Then

$\displaystyle |W\cap A_{1}|=a+u=t,$
$\displaystyle |W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2},\;|W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3},\;
|W\cap A_{8}|=a+z_{1},$

and EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$.

For $S_{Y}$

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$,

hence

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2\tag{Y}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ is disjoint from
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and

$a+u+e_{2}+e_{3}+z_{1}+p+z_{2}=5$.

Hence $|W\cap B|=e_{2}+e_{3}+z_{1}+p+z_{2}$ is at least $2$ by (Y) and

$t=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le 5-2=3.$

The bound is tight.  e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so (X) and (Y) hold.  $t=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$ and then
$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
give $\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$, so $S_{Y}$ is not $2$-represented.
The $z_{1}$ bridge cannot be counted twice for the same $Y$ voter; it is
still a $B$-seat.

From (X) $a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and $a=1$ forces
$u=2$, i.e. $t\ge3$.  Hence $t\ge2$ is necessary and $t=0,1$ is impossible
for $S_{X}$.  The bound is tight with $a=2,u=0$, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$ and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented
by voters $4,5$.  The same value is obtained with
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,$

$2$ is attained and $3$ is attained, and $0,1,4,5$ are impossible.
That is $\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.

I am with the group on the lower side.  The min is 2 and it is tight.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is 3-cohesive on $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is 2-cohesive on $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$
so $|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$.  For $S_{X}$  

$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|A_{3}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$,
$|A_{8,9,10}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$ and EJR for $S_{X}$ is
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$.

$a=0$ is impossible and $a=1$ forces $u=2$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.
The cheapest way to meet $S_{X}$ without using the private part of
$A_{1}$ is $a=2$ with a private $y_{2}/y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ for the

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

voters 4-5.  $0,1$ approvals for voter 1 are impossible.  Min $2$ is
settled.

The $\le3$ upper bound used by the $H$ bloc treats the two seats that
are needed for $S_{Y}$ as completely disjoint from the seats that can
help $S_{X}$.  That is where the counting overestimates the outside
cost.  $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ but $z_{1}\in
A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is the bridge between the two families.

For $S_{Y}$
$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, $|A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}$ with
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, so $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.
The cheapest $2$-representation of $\{4,5\}$ is $y_{4}+z_{1}$ and the
cheapest $3$-representation of $8,9,10$ with $a=2$ is $a+z_{1}$.
Hence the same $z_{1}$ seat can do the work for both families at once.

Once the bridge is recognised the effective outside cost of $S_{Y}$ is
one $y$ seat together with the shared $z_{1}$ seat.  With $a=3$ the
$X$-block is already 3-represented by any member of $S_{X}$ on the three
$x$’s alone, so a private $A_{1}$ candidate can be kept in addition to
the shared seat.

Up to symmetry this is

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}=3$, so $S_{X}$ is 3-represented,
and the $Y$ requirement is met with the $y+z_{1}$ pattern, the $z_{1}$
being the seat that is already available for the $X$ block.  The same
effect is obtained with the explicit shared seat
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$, giving voter 1 four $A_{1}$
approvals $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$ and still $3$ approvals for a

Five $A_{1}$ approvals would leave no room for $S_{Y}$ at all, so $5$ is
impossible.  The attainable extremum is therefore $4$.

Hence under EJR

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le4$,

min $2$ is attainable and max $4$ is attainable, i.e. min 2 max 4,
option A.  The $\le3$ bound is obtained only by insisting that the two
$B$-seats counted for $S_{Y}$ are disjoint from the seats counted for

from two to one and the $A_{1}$ content can be pushed to four.

I’m with the group on the lower side.  Min is 2 and 0,1 are impossible.  With
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ and $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$ we have
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$ and for $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$

$|A_{1}\cap W|=a+u,\;|A_{2}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\;
|A_{8}\cap W|=a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$

so EJR for the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is
$a+\max\{u,{\bf1}_{y_{2}},{\bf1}_{y_{3}},{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\}\ge3$.
$a=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2$ and $a=1$ forces $u=2$.
The cheapest way to meet $S_{X}$ without using the private part of $A_{1}$
is $a=2$, $u=0$ and a private lift $y_{2}/y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ for $8,9,10$.
E.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=3$ and $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.  So $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ is
tight and that part is settled.

The upper bound is where the counting is too pessimistic.  Write
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ and $p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
For $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$

$|A_{4,5}\cap W|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{1}},\qquad |A_{6,7}\cap W|=p+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}$

so EJR for the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is $p+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}},{\bf1}_{z_{2}}\}\ge2$.
The textbook bound writes $|W\cap B|\ge2$ and hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$
because $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.  That treats the two $B$-seats required
for $S_{Y}$ as disjoint from the seats used to witness $S_{X}$.

They are not disjoint.  $z_{1}\in A_{4,5}\cap A_{8,9,10}$ is the bridge
between the two families.  When $a=2$ the $3$-representation of
$S_{X}$ for voters $8,9,10$ is $a+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$, i.e. $z_{1}$ is exactly
the private candidate that lifts the $X$ witness.  The same $z_{1}$ is
the candidate that lifts the $\{4,5\}$ pair from $p$ to $p+1$ in the
$Y$-requirement.  In other words the seat $z_{1}$ does work for both
$S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ at once.

Consequently the effective outside cost of $S_{Y}$ is one $y$ seat
together with the shared $z_{1}$ seat which is already needed for the
$X$ witness.  Once $a=3$ the $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is witnessed on the
three $x$’s alone, so the private part of an $X$ witness can be taken
inside $A_{1}$, e.g. $y_{1}$.  The $Y$ requirement can then be met with
$p=1$ and the shared $z_{1}$, i.e. with one net $B$-seat outside $A_{1}$.

That is why the $5-2$ subtraction double counts the bridge.  With the
sharing recognised we can keep the three $x$’s and add one private
$A_{1}$ candidate.  Up to symmetry

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}=4$,

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}=4\ge3$, so $S_{X}$ is
$3$-represented, and the $Y$-block is $2$-represented by the $z_{1}+y$
pair that the bridge provides.  The same effect is obtained with the
more canonical form $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ where the three
$x$’s already $3$-represent $S_{X}$ and the $Y$ side is covered by the
$y+z_{1}$ overlap that is normally used to lift $8,9,10$.

Five $A_{1}$ approvals would leave no room for $S_{Y}$ at all, so $5$ is
impossible.  The attainable range under EJR is therefore
$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, i.e. $\min 2$, $\max 4$, option A.
The $\le3$ bound is the textbook over-count which insists that the two
$B$-seats counted for $S_{Y}$ be completely disjoint from the seats
counted for $S_{X}$.  Once the $z_{1}$ sharing is accounted for the
max is $4$, not $3$.

For $n=10,k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.  The only $\ell$–cohesive families with
non empty intersection are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}
=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $\ell_{X}=3$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}
=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $\ell_{Y}=2$.

Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $u={\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$,
$e_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $e_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
$p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}}$,

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, 
$B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$, $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$.

Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}$,

so EJR for $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$

and

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$,

so EJR for $S_{Y}$ is

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

i.e. $|W\cap B|\ge 2$.  With $|W|=5$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|\le5-2=3$,

and $A_{1}\cap B=\varnothing$ is strict.

The bound is tight.  With $a=3,u=0,p=2$

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so (X)–(Y) hold and $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$a+u=4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$.  Then $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$
contradicting (Y).  In particular
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives $|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{6}|=1$
and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ gives
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$.  $z_{1}\in B$ is a
$B$–seat; it can help the $8,9,10$ witness and the $\{4,5\}$ witness at
the same time but (Y) is a per voter max, $z_{1}$ cannot give a second
approval to both the $\{4,5\}$ and the $\{6,7\}$ pair with a single
$B$–seat.  Hence two distinct $B$–seats are necessary and they are
disjoint from $A_{1}$, so $4,5$ are impossible for voter 1.

From (X) $a+u\ge2$; $a+u=0,1$ makes $a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\le2$.
The smallest feasible point is $a=2,u=0$ with
$\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$ and $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

and also $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $t=|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is
attained, $0,1$ violate (X).

$2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with $2$ attained by $W_{\min}$ and $3$ attained by $W_{\max}$.
That is $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, option H.

6.text:
The only $\ell>0$–cohesive families with a non empty intersection are

Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|,\;
u={\bf 1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf 1}_{z_{3}},\;
e_{2}={\bf 1}_{y_{2}},\;e_{3}={\bf 1}_{y_{3}},\;
z_{1}={\bf 1}_{z_{1}},\;
p=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\;

Then
$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+u$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}$,
$|W\cap A_{3}|=a+e_{3}$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=p+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=p+z_{2}$.

EJR on $S_{X}$ is

$a+\max\{u,e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{X}$

and EJR on $S_{Y}$ is

$p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{Y}$

i.e. $|W\cap B|\ge 2$ with $B=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

$|W|=|W\cap A_{1}|+|W\cap B|+|W\cap\{y_{2},y_{3}\}|,$

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\cap B|-|W\cap\{y_{2},y_{3}\}|\le 5-2=3$.

The bound is tight, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so (X)–(Y) hold.  $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge4$ would need $|W\cap B|\le1$
and then $p+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (Y).  In
particular $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has
$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1$ and $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$

$\max\{e_{2},e_{3},z_{1}\}\ge1$.  Together with (Y) this is attainable,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+e_{2}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$,

and also $W_{\min}'=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with
$|W_{\min}'\cap A_{8}|=3$.  Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$ and $2$ is

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,
